###### Feature Story

##### May 3, 2020

# Up Close, Far Away

 By [Clive Paget](link_9)

![Image 3](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/Up-Close-Far-Away_Resized.jpg)
The Philadelphia Orchestra and Music Director Yannick Nézet-Séguin perform an audience-less concert at the Kimmel Center, March 12, 2020.

In Brief| During the time of coronavirus, with large-group gatherings banned and concert halls closed, streamed orchestra concerts are proliferating. For a brief period in March, orchestras performed their concerts to empty halls—the audiences were online. Here, a viewer’s perspective on the experience of orchestra livestreams that week. 

Share

[Facebook](link_0)[Twitter](link_0)

Download PDF[Download](link_10)

**League launches****_Symphony Spot_****, online destination for orchestra livestreams, videos, and more**

In early April, the League of American Orchestras unveiled _Symphony Spot_, an online hub of livestreams, videos, and digital learning events from League-member orchestras. As concert halls across the country go dark due to the COVID-19 pandemic, orchestras have given hope and solace to a quarantined public by making an unprecedented number of online performances and educational resources available free of charge. _Symphony Spot_ gives teachers, journalists, bloggers, and the general public a one-stop landing place to explore the inspiration that only orchestral music can provide. Visit [symphonyspot.org](link_11).

Change font size

[A Decrease font size.](https://symphony.org/features/up-close-far-away/# "Decrease font size")[A Reset font size.](https://symphony.org/features/up-close-far-away/# "Reset font size")[A Increase font size.](https://symphony.org/features/up-close-far-away/# "Increase font size")

This March, a global pandemic put a halt to live music as we know it. All around the globe, orchestras and musicians scrambled to adapt to the enforced closure of concert halls. Soloists performed in their own living rooms, and orchestras presented concerts in empty auditoriums as virtual viewers tuned in at Facebook, YouTube, and other streaming sites. But could performances without audiences truly feel “live”?

The Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra was among the first to join the stream of orchestra streams, announcing that their March 11 concert at the St. Louis Cathedral would be audience-free and streamed at the orchestra’s website and on TV station WLAE.com. The Philadelphia Orchestra played Beethoven on March 12 to an empty Verizon Hall, offering a free livestream on its website. The following night, Ohio’s Toledo Symphony Orchestra followed suit with a lively program of Lili Boulanger, Mahler, and Brahms, while New York’s Rochester Philharmonic switched online to stream their education concert to participating schools. Others livestreamed music for the first time, as the New Haven Symphony Orchestra did on March 5 at the Yale School of Music’s online portal.

> The Philadelphia Orchestra’s March 12 livestreamed concert made no attempt to hide the empty seats, lending an enormous poignancy to the event.

Watching a concert from the comfort of your own home has advantages. While some events are available only in real time, channel-hopping allows you to pick and mix from several programs. And while a bored dog demanding your attention might be an unwelcome distraction, there’s no pesky usher to stop you sipping a glass of wine or munching on popcorn (full disclosure: I have done both). Archived live-streamed concerts on websites and at Facebook and YouTube allow audiences to tune in and enjoy the music-making days, weeks, even years later.

The Philadelphia Orchestra’s March 12 performance of Beethoven’s Fifth and Sixth symphonies, livestreamed on Facebook, included surreal shots of players in tails tuning in front of empty seats, and a little nervous laughter when Concertmaster David Kim was greeted not with audience applause but silence. Then came a thoughtful address from Music Director Yannick Nézet-Séguin. “This music that we cherish, that we love, that inspires us, has survived hundreds of years of hardship and struggles,” he said, addressing the empty house—and, by extension, the viewers online. “I know that soon we are going to be back sharing this music with all of you as a great community, as a joyful event. But as we now share with you virtually, I know it will help us through these strange and difficult times for the entire world, helping us feel together on this beautiful planet Earth.”

> With live audience stats on the computer screen, it is possible to see how many people are tuning in to the livestream. I watched the South Carolina Philharmonic’s number of viewers rise to more than 1,000 mid-concert.

The livestream—which also included the world premiere of Iman Habibi’s Jeder Baum spricht, a piece about global warming—made no attempt to hide the empty seats, lending an enormous poignancy to the event. The view was exemplary, with sharp camerawork and excellent sound. Apart from the shot-to-shot segues, you could imagine you were in the best seat in the house. The first concert in a now-abandoned Beethoven symphony cycle, the performances were electrifying: crisp, urgent and alert. At the end, the orchestra stood in what felt like a moment of silent prayer.

### Global Virtual Stages

The chance to choose between orchestras across the U.S. and ensembles from all over the globe found me tuning in later the same evening to a live Berlin Philharmonic performance at the Berlin Philharmonie, led by Simon Rattle, the ​orchestra’s former chief conductor. Speaking on camera about the “wonderful, if strange evening,” Rattle drew parallels between Berio’s 1968 _Sinfonia_, composed in a time of social upheaval, and Bartók’s _Concerto for Orchestra_, written in America during a time of social isolation for the Hungarian exile, who famously spoke no English. Its folk-like themes, Rattle explained, expressed Bartók’s need to “retain a little piece of himself when he had no real contact with the outside world.”

Close-ups helped the ear untangle the highly complex music, and the sound was superb. Whether the balance was Rattle’s doing or the work of engineers, the clarity may well have exceeded the experience of sitting in the hall. With shots meticulously planned, this was state of the art, although the Philharmonie’s empty wraparound seating emphasized the loneliness of the event. “There’s often a small audience for contemporary music, but there’s always someone there,” quipped Rattle.

> Once the coronavirus crisis has passed, many orchestras will have learned lessons about livestreaming with intriguing implications for the future.

The following evening, I was able to catch the Boston Philharmonic Youth Orchestra’s March 12 Berlioz and Stravinsky program, which was streamed live on March 12, then archived for later streaming. Streamed in decent sound through Vimeo, BPYO’s cameras provided a vantage point as if sitting in a box high above the stage. Despite a half-hour of pre-concert milling around and a live feed that cut out during the crucial trumpet solo in _Petrushka_, it was a more rudimentary but no less inspiring affair. As conductor Benjamin Zander pointed out in his eloquent address, the Symphony Hall concert was being performed for the benefit of the young people themselves. “It’s important for you to play these pieces in this space,” he told the players, his back to the empty auditorium. “When my father got old and couldn’t go out anymore, he would listen to music on the radio, but only live music, never a recording. There is something about live music that shines, radiates, and creates a feeling of daring.”

### Listening Together

For smaller-budget orchestras, one potential upside of livestreams is a larger, more widespread audience. The South Carolina Philharmonic’s March 14 broadcast on both Facebook and YouTube was an excellent case in point. Music Director Morihiko Nakahara led a program that included Schumann’s Symphony No. 2 (a work that celebrated recovery after a period of illness) and Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 20 with seventeen-year-old Yerin Yang the elegant soloist. Frequent use of the longshot made this feel lonely, and silences between items were especially odd with only the orchestra to applaud the soloist. With live audience stats visible on the computer screen, it was possible to see how many people were tuning in to the livestream. I watched the South Carolina Philharmonic’s number of viewers rise from 90 (five minutes before the concert began) to more than 1,000 mid-concert. With most families staying put at home, it seems likely that those stats were higher, with more viewers watching the same livecast together.

Though the catchphrase of the moment is “social distancing,” many live-streamed concerts are in fact quite social: people watching on the same social media platform can chat (or listen to others chat) during the concert, in real time. The comment stream on YouTube during the South Carolina Philharmonic’s livestream made for fascinating reading: “Sounds great on my TV,” wrote more than one viewer. Frequent use of emojis became a little distracting, but the banter was good-natured: “Am I the only one feeling strange for talking during the concert?” typed one watcher. “Shhhh!” replied another. Best of all were interstate comments like, “Those of us under quarantine in New York state really appreciate this,” and “I’m watching from Spokane, WA.” Elbow bumps and an awkward moment over delivery of a bouquet during bows raised smiles and online thanks from as far afield as Utah, Massachusetts, and Illinois, with much talk of donations to the South Carolina Philharmonic’s musician relief fund.

Heart-warming though these live­streams were, a few days later it was mostly over as new social distancing rules prevented players coming together at all. Nevertheless, once the coronavirus crisis has passed, many orchestras will have learned a technological lesson with intriguing implications for the future.

This article originally appeared in the Spring 2020 issue of _Symphony_ magazine.

# [Catapulting into Classical](link_0)

## A headlong leap into music, history, and composing

![Image 1](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/cropped-yokoheader.png)

# A virtual orchestra performance and more great free concerts

[March 25, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/25/a-virtual-orchestra-performance-and-more-great-free-concerts/ "1:58 pm") by [Chris Gallant](link_12)[2 Comments](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/25/a-virtual-orchestra-performance-and-more-great-free-concerts/#comments)

[![Image 2: illustration of the seating chart of an orchestra with each instrument in its own box](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/isolatedorchestra001.jpg?w=212&h=150)](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/isolatedorchestra001.jpg)

Musicians can’t _not_ make music. And when creative people, well, get creative, wonderful things can happen. What does an orchestra do when everyone has to stay home?

Watch the [Toronto Symphony Orchestra play Aaron Copland’s _Appalachian Spring_](link_13).

[Video 1](link_14)

Seeing this video made me think of a comment by artist Janet Cardiff, highlighted in [my _Virtual Choirs_ post](link_15). She said that visitors to her sound installation would frequently walk directly up to a speaker projecting a singer’s voice, something that you could not do with a live choir. The visitors literally got close to the music, hearing each singer’s voice in a way that you cannot do under normal circumstances. In the Toronto Symphony Orchestra video, you can see, frequently close up, each musician, a view that you cannot get, certainly at live performances, and even in recorded concerts. They are all wearing different clothing, you can see them as individuals. And there is something very warm in that.

I can only hope that the resourcefulness that is now being displayed during this crisis will not be forgotten once the crisis is past, and that we will find new ways to bring more music to more people in more venues, and find ways for musicians to be justly compensated for bringing their music directly to their listeners and viewers.

So, let’s hear some more music!

[Here is an article from the CBC providing details on “6 cool classical concerts to watch right now.”](link_16)

[L’Orchestre symphonique de Montreal](link_17) is streaming concerts from its archives every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 8:00PM ET (GMT -4).

At this link you can see the [Vancouver Symphony Orchestra perform Beethoven’s Fourth Piano Concerto and his Sixth Symphony “Pastorale”](link_18). It is a top-notch performance.

If you find great performances or live concerts I haven’t discovered, be sure to share them with everyone in the comments. Thanks!

# A virtual orchestra performance and more great free concerts

[March 25, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/25/a-virtual-orchestra-performance-and-more-great-free-concerts/ "1:58 pm") by [Chris Gallant](link_12)[2 Comments](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/25/a-virtual-orchestra-performance-and-more-great-free-concerts/#comments)

[![Image 2: illustration of the seating chart of an orchestra with each instrument in its own box](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/isolatedorchestra001.jpg?w=212&h=150)](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/isolatedorchestra001.jpg)

Musicians can’t _not_ make music. And when creative people, well, get creative, wonderful things can happen. What does an orchestra do when everyone has to stay home?

Watch the [Toronto Symphony Orchestra play Aaron Copland’s _Appalachian Spring_](link_13).

[Video 1](link_14)

Seeing this video made me think of a comment by artist Janet Cardiff, highlighted in [my _Virtual Choirs_ post](link_15). She said that visitors to her sound installation would frequently walk directly up to a speaker projecting a singer’s voice, something that you could not do with a live choir. The visitors literally got close to the music, hearing each singer’s voice in a way that you cannot do under normal circumstances. In the Toronto Symphony Orchestra video, you can see, frequently close up, each musician, a view that you cannot get, certainly at live performances, and even in recorded concerts. They are all wearing different clothing, you can see them as individuals. And there is something very warm in that.

I can only hope that the resourcefulness that is now being displayed during this crisis will not be forgotten once the crisis is past, and that we will find new ways to bring more music to more people in more venues, and find ways for musicians to be justly compensated for bringing their music directly to their listeners and viewers.

So, let’s hear some more music!

[Here is an article from the CBC providing details on “6 cool classical concerts to watch right now.”](link_16)

[L’Orchestre symphonique de Montreal](link_17) is streaming concerts from its archives every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 8:00PM ET (GMT -4).

At this link you can see the [Vancouver Symphony Orchestra perform Beethoven’s Fourth Piano Concerto and his Sixth Symphony “Pastorale”](link_18). It is a top-notch performance.

If you find great performances or live concerts I haven’t discovered, be sure to share them with everyone in the comments. Thanks!

# How Louisiana Orchestras Are Innovating to Connect With Audiences

![Image 3](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/louisiana-phil-new-marigny-theatre.jpg)
The Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra in a recent performance at New Orleans’ New Marigny Theatre. Photo source: Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra.

Share

[Facebook](link_0)[Twitter](link_0)

Change font size

[A Decrease font size.](https://symphony.org/how-louisiana-orchestras-are-innovating-to-connect-with-audiences/# "Decrease font size")[A Reset font size.](https://symphony.org/how-louisiana-orchestras-are-innovating-to-connect-with-audiences/# "Reset font size")[A Increase font size.](https://symphony.org/how-louisiana-orchestras-are-innovating-to-connect-with-audiences/# "Increase font size")

In Tuesday’s (9/22) [Nola.com](link_9)(Louisiana), Rich Collins writes, “The Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra was rehearsing Johannes Brahms’ Symphony No. 4 in E minor recently … The music sounded amazing … but conductor Matthew Kraemer still paused the [musicians] from time to time to make adjustments … A similar process of trial and error is happening on a much larger scale at the LPO itself and at Louisiana’s other professional orchestras as they strive to sell tickets and keep donations flowing … In Louisiana, that means sharing the stage with musicians from other genres, showcasing music from popular movie scores and commissioning original works that highlight jazz, Cajun and other regional sounds. It also means playing lots of gigs in nontraditional environments, embracing online video content and finding other ways to build awareness and excitement … Audiences have become ‘omnivorous,’ according to Rachel Rossos Gallant, vice president of marketing and membership at the League of American Orchestras. ‘They still want the classics, but they also want other genres, so having cross-genre programming is really helpful…. They are [performing] where people are,’ Rossos Gallant said. ‘It helps build relationships with community, and it helps with fundraising. It’s also part of the nonprofit mission to build something communal, especially at a time when things can be divisive.’ ”

# Cooped up at home? Here are 6 cool classical concerts to watch right now

Enrich your alone time by streaming these recent performances by Canadian musicians.

## Enrich your alone time by streaming these recent performances by Canadian musicians

[Robert Rowat](link_18) · CBC Music · Posted: Mar 18, 2020 10:02 AM EDT | Last Updated: March 18, 2020

![Image 2](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5496653,1584112674000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C282%2C5472%2C3078%29%3B)

Violinist Timothy Chooi won 2nd prize at the 2019 Queen Elisabeth Competition in Brussels.(Ryan Brandenberg)

## Social Sharing

With symphony orchestras, opera companies and chamber music societies cancelling performances due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and with citizens being urged to adopt social distancing to prevent the spread of the virus, classical concert life in most parts of Canada has ground to a halt.

*   [5 ways to support Canada's musicians during the coronavirus pandemic](link_19)
*   [An up-to-date list of Canadian live streams to watch during COVID-19](link_20)
*   [Updated How has COVID-19 impacted Canadian musicians and fans?](link_21)

It's a troubling situation for performing artists, most of whom are facing a loss of income. A growing movement is urging ticket-holders to donate their tickets, if they can afford to do so, rather than request a refund for cancelled concerts, as a way of alleviating the financial pressure on musicians.

We're hopeful that things will return to normal soon, but until then, the internet provides a temporary solution for classical music lovers. Here are six concerts,recorded during the past year and featuring Canadian classical musicians, that you can stream from home.

* * *

## Louis Lortie plays Chopin's Études

Last October, pianist Lortie gave an all-Chopin recital at Venice's La Fenice opera house, playing both the Op. 10 and Op. 25 sets of Études.With his robust tone and passionate interpretation,he kept the audience on the edge of their seats.

[Video 1](link_22)

[Video 2](link_23)

* * *

## Timothy Chooi plays Grieg

En route to his second prize at the Queen Elisabeth Competition in Brussels last May, Chooi played Grieg's Violin Sonata No. 3 with pianist Takashi Sato. An assured performance that wowed the crowd with nuanced phrasing and astonishing lyricism.

[Video 3](link_24)

* * *

## Against the Grain Theatre presents La bohème in a bar

Last fall, Against the Grain Theatre presented a scaled-down version of Puccini's _La bohème_. Set in modern times, sung in English by an age-appropriate cast and performed in bars rather than opera houses, this opera on a shoe-string budget caused a sensation on tour stops from Alberta to Ontario. CBC live streamed a performance from Toronto's Tranzac Club.

*   [Meet the pianist who's doing the job of an entire orchestra (and conductor!) on a Puccini opera tour](link_25)

[Video 4](link_26)

* * *

## James Ehnes plays Bruch in Auckland

On May 30, Ehnes was the guest of the Auckland Philharmonia Orchestra to play Bruch's Violin Concerto No. 1 with conductor Giordano Bellincampi. Stick around for the encore: a masterful rendition of Ysaÿe's Sonata No. 3 for solo violin.

[Video 5](link_27)

* * *

## McGill Symphony Orchestra plays Mahler's 5th

Closer to home, the McGill Symphony Orchestra filled Montreal's St. Jean Baptiste Church last March with the heroic strains of Mahler's Symphony No. 5 under the direction of longtime artistic director Alexis Hauser. During the ovation that greets the symphony's finale, principal trumpeter Peixiang Li gets extra applause for his rock-solid solos.

[Video 6](link_28)

* * *

## Royal Conservatory of Music's Academy Chamber Orchestra plays Tchaikovsky

The Phil and Eli Taylor Performance Academy for Young Artists is an elite training program at Toronto's Royal Conservatory of Music. From its December 2019 concert at Mazzoleni Hall, the Academy Chamber Orchestra's performance of Tchaikovsky's Serenade for Strings — without a conductor! — was a highlight.

[Video 7](link_29)

## A headlong leap into music, history, and composing

![Image 1](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/cropped-yokoheader.png)

# Virtual Choirs

[March 23, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/23/virtual-choirs/ "9:03 pm") by [Chris Gallant](link_12)[Leave a comment](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/23/virtual-choirs/#respond)

[![Image 2: grid of 16 boxes, each containing a stick figure choir singer](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/virtualchoirproto001.jpg?w=235&h=198)](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/virtualchoirproto001.jpg)

At the moment, choirs cannot sing together. But today, I have for you two examples of virtual choirs.

Composer [Eric Whitacre](link_13) got the idea of a virtual choir “gathering” to sing his composition _Luz Aurumque_. The result is stunning. [Here is the virtual choir singing _Lux Aurumque_](link_14).[You can read about the virtual choir here](link_15).

[Video 1](link_16)

Artist Janet Cardiff had a different idea. Cardiff recorded a choir singing Thomas Tallis’s _Spem in alium,_ a motet for 40 voices.[You can read more about _Spem in alium_ here](link_17). Each singer had their own microphone. She then tuned the result into a sound installation. The voice of each individual singer comes from its own speaker. While no human singers are present in the installation, it is a profoundly human experience. I encourage you to watch [this video about the sound installation](link_18). [Here is an excerpt of Cardiff’s installation](link_19).

[Video 2](link_20)

And because we all need this now (_Spem_ means “hope” in Latin), [here is the complete _Spem in alium_](link_21).

[Video 3](link_22)

# [Catapulting into Classical](link_0)

## A headlong leap into music, history, and composing

![Image 1](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/cropped-yokoheader.png)

# Virtual Choirs

[March 23, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/23/virtual-choirs/ "9:03 pm") by [Chris Gallant](link_12)[Leave a comment](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/23/virtual-choirs/#respond)

[![Image 2: grid of 16 boxes, each containing a stick figure choir singer](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/virtualchoirproto001.jpg?w=235&h=198)](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/virtualchoirproto001.jpg)

At the moment, choirs cannot sing together. But today, I have for you two examples of virtual choirs.

Composer [Eric Whitacre](link_13) got the idea of a virtual choir “gathering” to sing his composition _Luz Aurumque_. The result is stunning. [Here is the virtual choir singing _Lux Aurumque_](link_14).[You can read about the virtual choir here](link_15).

[Video 1](link_16)

Artist Janet Cardiff had a different idea. Cardiff recorded a choir singing Thomas Tallis’s _Spem in alium,_ a motet for 40 voices.[You can read more about _Spem in alium_ here](link_17). Each singer had their own microphone. She then tuned the result into a sound installation. The voice of each individual singer comes from its own speaker. While no human singers are present in the installation, it is a profoundly human experience. I encourage you to watch [this video about the sound installation](link_18). [Here is an excerpt of Cardiff’s installation](link_19).

[Video 2](link_20)

And because we all need this now (_Spem_ means “hope” in Latin), [here is the complete _Spem in alium_](link_21).

[Video 3](link_22)

Music inspires us, strengthens us, and brings us together. Early in the pandemic, the League of American Orchestras began gathering online offerings by friends and members. This Performance Directory was maintained between April 2020 and September 2021. [**ASO36 REVIVAL Season**](link_17) begins in September and features seven concerts through May 2021. A season packed with inspiring arrangements, The Revival Season will fill your soul. Revive with us in person or through LiveStreaming this season.

#### [**American Composers Orchestra**](link_66)

American Composers Orchestra (ACO)centers composers in all that it does.Activities focus on creating, performing, and promoting orchestral music by American composers.

[**Concerts**](link_67)&[**Composer to Composer Conversations**](link_67)-Orchestra lovers and new music enthusiasts alike will find chances to discover new artists and works through ACO’s virtual and in-person concerts and Composer to Composer conversations, which feature composers speaking about their works and leading creative lives.

American Composers Orchestra (ACO) continues its series of [**Composer to Composer Talks**](link_68), which features major American composers in conversation with each other about their work and leading a creative life. The intergenerational discussions will begin by exploring a single work with one composer interviewing the other. Attendees will gain insight to each work’s genesis, sound, influence on the American orchestral canon, and be invited to ask questions of the artists.

For this installment, Jonathan Bailey Holland talks with Alvin Singleton about his work BluesKonzert, a triple commission from 1995 by the Detroit, Houston, and Kansas City symphony orchestras. The talk will be hosted by ACO’s Artistic Director Derek Bermel, live-streamed and available to watch for seven days after the event.

Of BluesKonzert, Michael Fleming writes in the program note, “Vernacular and classical traditions have often cross-pollinated in American music, both in performance and composition. A case in point is BluesKonzert, which mixes musical bloodlines as neatly as its title does language. Konzert is a German term that can mean either ‘concert,’ as in a musical program, or ‘concerto,’ as in a work for solo instrument and orchestra. Singleton, who trained in both classical music and jazz, is perfectly positioned to exploit such ambiguities and crossovers.”

[**EarShot Readings**](link_69)&[**Professional Development Webinar**](link_67)-Emerging and aspiring composers are invited to online professional development webinars, and should keep their eyes open for open calls to apply for EarShot Readings and fellowships across the country.

[**YouTube**](link_70)-ACO’s YouTube channel is a virtual treasure trove of short concerts,composer portrait interviews,professional development webinars, and instructional clips for middle and high school students.

-American Composers Orchestra

To support American Composers Orchestra, you can submit a [**donation**](link_71) online.

[**Facebook**](link_72) -[**Instagram**](link_73) -[**Twitter**](link_74)

#### [**American Youth Symphony**](link_75)

The American Youth Symphony is dedicated to making great music accessible by sharing concert videos on the [**AYS YouTube Channel**](link_76), as well as new practice videos for younger musicans. AYS is showcasing legendary past performances on social media in #ThrowbackTunes features. Join the monthly[**AYS e-news**](link_77)or visit[**www.aysymphony.org**](link_75)for announcements of upcoming virtual content and new content on the[**AYS Amplifies blog**](link_78).

-American Youth Symphony

To support the American Youth Symphony, you can submit at [**donation**](link_79) online.

[**Facebook**](link_80) - [**Instagram**](link_81) - [**Twitter**](link_82) - [**YouTube**](link_83)

* * *

![Image 16: ASO Vertical logo.jpeg](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5e751ede8fddbf70270e01b6/1587753372005-JI423AVMKZZROU5E4XVV/ASO+Vertical+logo.jpeg)

#### [**Anchorage Symphony Orchestra**](link_84)

**Great Music for Every Life** - It's the most important thing the Anchorage Symphony can bring to our community right now. And while gathering in our Atwood Concert Hall performance home at the Alaska Center for the Performing Arts isn't possible, we're proud to continue sharing art with our friends and neighbors. Visit AnchorageSymphony.org and our social media platforms for regularly-updated content featuring:

[**ASO on Demand**](link_85)- After launching our first-ever Virtual Season Finale on April 4th, we're continuing to share archived concert videos and photos, as well as new “mini-concerts” directly from the homes of ASO musicians. Watch for a few big virtual concert events during this unprecedented period.

# T - Z

Enjoy these online offerings by members and friends of the League of American Orchestras. Music inspires us, strengthens us, and brings us together; please consider a donation to your local orchestra in these difficult times.

#### [**Tampa Bay Symphony**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCxvEx_s0DqLfNviOA9SBWFg)

The Tampa Bay Symphony is an 80+ member volunteer orchestra that has been described as "a hidden jewel." Videos of pre-pandemic full orchestra performances can be found at our [**YouTube site**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCxvEx_s0DqLfNviOA9SBWFg), or you can visit [**TampaBaySymphony.org**](http://tampabaysymphony.org/) for complete information on our organization.

-Tampa Bay Symphony

#### [**Tippet Rise Art Center**](https://tippetrise.org/)

[**Tippet Rise & Friends at Home: Monthly Video Streams**](http://tippetrise.org/virtual-events) - A monthly video stream which shares video of previously unreleased concerts from past seasons.

The concerts will be made available for streaming each month at 6pm MT on a Thursday and some will feature special intermission content, conversation with musicians, or segments showcasing some of Tippet Rise’s monumental outdoor sculptures and architectural structures, as well as other scenes from the 12,000-acre art center. The streaming series is available on the Tippet Rise website at[tippetrise.org/virtual-events](http://tippetrise.org/virtual-events). Upcoming concerts will also take place on Thursdays; dates to be announced.

-Tippet Rise Art Center

[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/Tippet-Rise-Art-Center-402432033200609) - [**Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/tippet.rise/) - [**Twitter**](https://twitter.com/TippetRise) - [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCxuB4LkBOTSxwBK4l1JMo0Q)

#### [**Toledo Symphony Orchestra**](https://www.toledosymphony.com/)

[**Website**](https://www.toledosymphony.com/) - The Toledo Symphony Orchestra is committed to safely bringing the Toledo community together in lasting musical moments.

In addition to in-person events, the TSO has invested in a state-of-the-art, easy-to-use streaming platform to bring live performances to local, national, and global audiences. The TSO has become more accessible than ever before, offering live and on-demand performances through a variety of ways, including apps on Roku and Apple TV. The platform includes both free and paid content that’s available to watch anywhere, at any time.

-Toledo Symphony Orchestra

#### [**Toronto Symphony Orchestra**](https://www.tso.ca/)

[**TSO at the Drive-In**](https://www.tso.ca/drive-in) is back by popular demand! September 24 & 25 and October 1 & 2, we’re presenting hour-long, crowd-pleasing, and contactless programs, performed live at CityView Drive-In in Toronto. Surrender to Mozart’s passionate Symphony No. 40 in your station wagon, and clap along to our celebration of all things Pride in your coupe!

[**Mistatim**](https://www.redskytv.com/products/mistatim-for-home-family-viewing) - Red Sky Performance and the Toronto Symphony Orchestra (TSO) have collaborated on a digital reimagining of Red Sky’s award-winning stage production for young people, Mistatim, in association with Crow’s Theatre. Indigenous music creators and TSO musicians worked in partnership to create new musical additions to the play’s score. The video will be available for viewing for schools and classrooms and the general public, beginning on September 30, 2021, Canada’s first National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

An unforgettable story of reconciliation, Mistatim tells the story of a wild horse who encounters Calvin on his ranch and Speck on her reservation. A simple wooden fence is all that separates them but in many ways, they are worlds apart—until Mistatim turns their worlds upside down and the truest of friendships is forged.

Mistatim is available for viewing September 30–October 18, 2021.

-Toronto Symphony Orchestra

#### [**Tulsa Symphony Orchestra**](https://tulsasymphony.org/)

Get to know the Tulsa Symphony Orchestra! Each week, we will highlight two of our orchestra members as they bring viewers into their daily lives as musicians, as artists, and as people. With the help of Ken Busby, beloved Tulsan and Tulsa Symphony ambassador, “Musician Moment” will share interesting facts about our musicians, from a musician’s favorite recipe to when they first fell in love with music. Enjoy the healing power of music as each share their talents during this special streamed performance. This series will run on Saturdays and Wednesdays at 10:00 AM CST on the Tulsa Symphony [**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/TulsaSymphony/) and [**YouTube**](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCc9PWLIQMsLyMwupM0YZ-WA) pages.

-Tulsa Symphony Orchestra

#### [**University of North Carolina School of the Arts**](https://www.uncsa.edu/performances/at-home/index.aspx)

The School of Music at UNC School of the Arts has launched its reimagined fall performance season with a robust series of livestreams featuring guest artists, student ensembles, faculty performances, and more. Performances will be available on demand following each livestream. View the [**calendar of upcoming performances**](https://www.uncsa.edu/performances/index.aspx?filter=music&start=0).

[**UNCSA at Home**](https://www.uncsa.edu/performances/at-home/index.aspx "https://www.uncsa.edu/performances/at-home/index.aspx")- UNCSA stages might be dark, but our students and faculty are still bringing light to our community through their art as they continue their training at home.   
Although our performance season was cut short, we’re bringing you online performances and video features until we can be back together in person. Now, more than ever, the world needs artists, and ours are the future. Check back here for more that will be added over the coming weeks.

-University of North Carolina School of the Arts

#### [**Ural Philharmonic Orchestra / Sverdlovsk Philharmonic**](https://sgaf.ru/)

We offer daily broadcasts of the recordings of concerts that took place in Sverdlovsk Philharmonic, Yekaterinburg, Russia with participation of the resident orchestras - Ural Philharmonic Orchestra, Chief Conductor and Artistic Director - Dmitry Liss, Ural Youth Symphony Orchestra, Chief Conductor - Enkhe, Yekaterinburg Philharmonic Choir, Artistic Director and Choirmaster - Andrei Petrenko, and Guest Artists and Orchestras from Russia and abroad.Our full HD streams are free of charge and take place at 6.30 pm (EDT+9) on work days and at 6.00 pm (EDT+9) on weekends at [**www.sgaf.ru**](http://www.sgaf.ru/). We announce the events additionally at the Orchestra's FB page [**https://www.facebook.com/UralPhilharmonicOrchestra**](https://www.facebook.com/UralPhilharmonicOrchestra).

Stay well and enjoy our music weeks with #philharmonicathome!

-Ural Philharmonic Orchestra / Sverdlovsk Philharmonic

#### [**Utah Symphony**](https://utahsymphony.org/)

Performances are available for streaming through [**USUO: On Demand**](https://usuo.org/on-demand/)

Utah Symphony remains committed to safely and creatively uplift and educate using music as an outlet and escape. We continue to create and connect a community of music lovers drawn together in difficult times through the power of music.

Utah Symphony's Education Department has migrated resources online in [**School from Home**](https://utahsymphony.org/education/school-from-home/) to help support teachers, parents and students in our suddenly digital-only learning environment.

Past performances and recordings, and the “Ghost Light Podcast” are available for on demand streaming in the [**Listening Room**](https://utahsymphony.org/explore/playlists/listening-room/).

-Utah Symphony

#### [**The Venice Symphony**](https://www.thevenicesymphony.org/)

## A headlong leap into music, history, and composing

![Image 1](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/cropped-yokoheader.png)

# A little Levit-y

[April 1, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/04/01/a-little-levit-y/ "11:55 am") by [Chris Gallant](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/author/catapultingintoclassical/ "View all posts by Chris Gallant")[3 Comments](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/04/01/a-little-levit-y/#comments)

No April Fools foolishness today. But a little fun.

I hope everyone is staying home and staying safe out there. After a while though, you might be wondering what to do with your time. [Here’s one idea](https://twitter.com/igorpianist/status/1244003365849305089). This is pianist [Igor Levit](https://www.igor-levit.com/). The caption is “And what’s Corona doing to you?” If you go to [his Twitter feed](https://twitter.com/igorpianist), you can check out his wonderful mini-concerts.

> Und was macht Corona so mit Euch? [pic.twitter.com/qO4Qx1pv6l](https://t.co/qO4Qx1pv6l)
> 
> 
> — Igor Levit (@igorpianist) [March 28, 2020](https://twitter.com/igorpianist/status/1244003365849305089?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

In other news, now that all the pesky humans are staying inside in Llandudno, the goats have taken over the streets. Boars are strolling through Bergamo. What could be next? [Could there be trouble brewing?](https://twitter.com/davidschneider/status/1244939562910089217)

> The Llandudno goats are so much better with a West Side Story soundtrack.
> 
> 
> (thanks to [@AndrewStuart](https://twitter.com/AndrewStuart?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) and the Bergamo boars) [pic.twitter.com/A71FumsGNa](https://t.co/A71FumsGNa)
> 
> 
> — David Schneider (@davidschneider) [March 31, 2020](https://twitter.com/davidschneider/status/1244939562910089217?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Personally, I’m thinking more of [Prokofiev’s Montagues and Capulets](https://youtu.be/8VY-A7GVLyQ?start=80). Mute the above video and try it!

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8VY-A7GVLyQ)

_______

A tip of the hat to Clara Parkes of [_The Daily Respite_](https://dailyrespite.substack.com/) who blogged about the Llandudno goats video.

Title: An up-to-date list of Canadian live streams to watch during COVID-19 URL Source: https://www.cbc.ca/music/an-up-to-date-list-of-canadian-live-streams-to-watch-during-covid-19-1.5500113 Published Time: 2020-05-05T14:43:24.048Z Markdown Content: [Skip to Main Content](https://www.cbc.ca/music/an-up-to-date-list-of-canadian-live-streams-to-watch-during-covid-19-1.5500113#content)[Accessibility Help](https://cbchelp.cbc.ca/hc/en-ca/categories/31606111569053-Accessibility) [Menu](https://www.cbc.ca/sitemap)[CBC Gem](https://gem.cbc.ca/)[CBC Listen](https://www.cbc.ca/listen) [](https://www.cbc.ca/) Search [Search](https://www.cbc.ca/search) Sign In ##### Quick Links * [News](https://www.cbc.ca/news) * [Sports](https://www.cbc.ca/sports) * [Radio](https://www.cbc.ca/radio) * [Music](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Listen Live](https://www.cbc.ca/listen/live-radio) * [TV](https://www.cbc.ca/television) * [Watch](https://gem.cbc.ca/) * [music music](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Read](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Watch](https://www.cbc.ca/music/watch) * [Events](https://www.cbc.ca/music/events) * [Explore](https://www.cbc.ca/music/explore) * [Listen Live](https://www.cbc.ca/listen/live-radio) * [Junos](https://www.cbc.ca/music/junos) * [Eurovision](https://www.cbc.ca/music/eurovision) * More An up-to-date list of Canadian live streams to watch during COVID-19 | CBC Music Loaded [Music](https://www.cbc.ca/music) # An up-to-date list of Canadian live streams to watch during COVID-19 This week: Jully Black, Shred Kelly and others perform from their homes. ## This week: Jully Black, Shred Kelly and others perform from their homes [Holly Gordon](https://www.cbc.ca/music/author/holly-gordon-1.5133796), [Jesse Kinos-Goodin](https://www.cbc.ca/author/jesse-kinos-goodin-1.4558986) · CBC Music · Posted: May 05, 2020 10:43 AM EDT | Last Updated: June 8, 2020 ![Image 2](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5441515,1580137280000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C605%2C5760%2C3240%29%3B) Jully Black performs on June 12 as part of the DT Concert Series, which is run out of the Dominion Telegraph venue in Paris, Ont. (Vivian Rashotte/CBC) ## Social Sharing comments _Editor's note: as of Tuesday, June 9, this post will no longer be updated._ This time of social distancing is necessary but difficult, putting a big strain on people whose livelihoods depend on bringing people together. And while musicians have been cancelling tours and plans daily, they still want to bring their art to the masses— and hopefully drum up some revenue in the process, from fans who are able to contribute during this tough financial time. * [We asked a music therapist how to relieve anxiety caused by social distancing](https://www.cbc.ca/music/we-asked-a-music-therapist-how-to-relieve-anxiety-caused-by-social-distancing-1.5504973) * [20 incredible music films you can stream online right now](https://www.cbc.ca/music/20-incredible-music-films-you-can-stream-online-right-now-1.5526547) * [How COVID-19 is changing the way we listen to music](https://www.cbc.ca/music/how-covid-19-is-changing-the-way-we-listen-to-music-1.5546533) * ['I am mentally preparing for my career to stop': what it's like to be a musician right now](https://www.cbc.ca/music/i-am-mentally-preparing-for-my-career-to-stop-what-it-s-like-to-be-a-musician-right-now-1.5524202) As the coronavirus pandemic progresses, CBC Music will be keeping an eye out for Canadian musicians' live streams and efforts to keep creating while most people are self-isolating. We'll keep updating this list as often as possible, but if something's missing please let us know via Twitter: [@CBCMusic](https://twitter.com/CBCMusic?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor). ## This week * June 9, 4 p.m. ET: Tune in to the announcement of the Royal Conservatory of Music's 2020-21 concert season, which boasts appearances by Kronos Quartet, Dianne Reeves, Skratch Bastid and others. Watch on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/events/181257306418332/). * June 11, 7 p.m. ET: the Minanzi Mbira Band perform a blend of mbira, djembe and Shona-inspired songs. This is the group's first online performance. Tickets are $6 via [Side Door](https://sidedooraccess.com/shows/K6wtxR4CLHlseDFJDQdl). * June 12, 9 p.m. ET: Jully Black performs as part of the DT Concert Series, which is run out of the Dominion Telegraph venue in Paris, Ont. All tickets are available at[DTConcertSeries.com](https://www.dtconcertseries.com/) and the concert will be live streamed via Zoom. * June 11, 1 p.m. ET: Shred Kelly hosts an intimate pre-release listening party for the band's upcoming album,_Like a Rising Sun_, out June 19. Tickets are $10, via [Side Door](https://sidedooraccess.com/shows/m2r2rww17yjQ6DiYEgsS). ## Week of June 15 to 21 * June 18, 3 p.m. ET: Toronto-based Xenia Concerts, a series designed specifically for autistic audience members, presents the fourth live stream in their series, this time featuring Angela Park. According to the[Xenia Concerts website](https://xeniaconcerts.com/2020/03/29/xenia-livestream-concerts/), "The concerts will feature many of the same elements that are present at a typical live Xenia Concert, including stretch breaks, and a downloadable program with program checklist that you can use to follow along during the performance." Watch it via[Facebook Live](https://www.facebook.com/xeniaconcertsinc/). * June 19, 7:30 p.m. ET: Montreal's Frase performs as part of Ballytobin Live from the Isabel Online Summer Music Festival. Watch via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pg/queensuisabel/live). * June 20, 3 p.m. ET: Sadaf Amini performs as part of Ballytobin Live from the Isabel Online Summer Music Festival. Watch via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pg/queensuisabel/live). * June 20, 9 p.m. ET: Royal Wood performs as part of the DT Concert Series, which is run out of the Dominion Telegraph venue in Paris, Ont. All tickets are available at[DTConcertSeries.com](https://www.dtconcertseries.com/) and the concert will be live streamed via Zoom. * June 21, 7:30 p.m. ET:Leanne Betasamosake Simpson and her band perform as part of Ballytobin Live from the Isabel Online Summer Music Festival. Watch via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/pg/queensuisabel/live). ## Week of June 22 to 28 * June 25, 8 a.m. ET: Pianist Angela Hewitt performs music by J.S. Bach, including English Suite No. 6 and French Suite No. 5, live from Wigmore Hall in London, England. Watch on [Wigmore Hall's website](https://wigmore-hall.org.uk/watch-listen/live-stream). * June 25, 7:30 p.m. AT: tune in for Online Encore: Brahms with Holly Mathieson, a rebroadcast from Symphony Nova Scotia, originally having taken place on Nov.7, 2019, at the Rebecca Cohn Auditorium in Halifax. Watch via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/events/166788534769742/). * June 27, 7:30 p.m.: Guitarist Adam Cicchillitti plays music by Scarlatti, Barrios, Roux, Rodrigo and Tansman. It's the seventh instalment in the Concerts for the End of Time series. Tune in on [Facebook Live](https://www.facebook.com/events/975314459587271/). * June 29, 9 p.m. ET: Skydiggers performs as part of the DT Concert Series, which is run out of the Dominion Telegraph venue in Paris, Ont. All tickets are available at[DTConcertSeries.com](https://www.dtconcertseries.com/) and the concert will be live streamed via Zoom. ## Fall 2020 * Oct. 9-17: the Celtic Colours International Festival will take place at everyone's home this year, with programming details to come. Get more information via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=884909321988133). ## Ongoing * May 25 to June 7, 7:30 p.m. AT daily:the 2020 Scotia Festival of Music, a 14-day free festival of chamber music, moves to[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/scotiafestivalofmusic/photos/a.368220516532255/3070707349616878/?type=3&theater). * Thursdays, 7 p.m. ET: Jess Moskaluke hosts a live show via [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/B_VSnyng3lN/), with special guests announced weekly. * Saturdays, 12 p.m. PT: Dan Mangan hosts a weekly Side Door show called #Quarantunes. Tickets are $6, and you can buy them via [Side Door](https://sidedooraccess.com/shows/RCeSH1g8JdjfPambIOyL). * Daily, 1 p.m ET: Arkells frontman Max Kerman offers up a music class on the band's[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/arkellsmusic/)page, complete with fan call-ins and special guests. * May 15-June 30: Halifax festival Every Seeker, formerly OBEY Convention, is moving its 2020 edition online, but instead of one weekend of shows it's now more than a month-long series of artists' creations. Called Emergent Response, the lineup includes Aquakultre, Joyfultalk, Kwento, Kevin Howes and more. Head to [everyseeker.com](https://www.everyseeker.com/) for details and the schedule, updated every week. * Sundays, 4 p.m. AT: Danny Michel performs his weekly show Live From Lockdown via [Side Door](https://sidedooraccess.com/shows/KBEoZNEIAnNSprWWxmXq). Tickets are $7. * Daily, 7 p.m. ET: James Barker Band performs #sixoclockshadowsessions on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/jamesbarkerband/) and [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/jamesbarkerband/). * Wednesdays, 3 p.m. ET: Paper Beat Scissors performs weekly from his Montreal home. Watch via [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UChpQTEcbHLrVIqzPJb1SYDQ). > Join @paperbeat every Wednesday on YouTube for a very special series of intimate performances from his home in Montreal. Come for the chats, requests, heckles and guests!

Facebook Event: https://t.co/fGby2qvcV5
Watch: https://t.co/vadvRcKvwC
Donate: https://t.co/qsI74JuV1zpic.twitter.com/QkxZHgVhdb > > —[@envision_mgmt](https://twitter.com/envision_mgmt/status/1260604384708263936) * Wednesdays, 7:30 p.m. ET: Deidrey Francois performs her Sofa SongFest every week, an hour-long set for singing, dancing and song requests. Via her [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC6RuzI0wzGwF_SwKaMA7dtQ) channel. * Nightly, 9 p.m. ET: Jim Clayton has been performing nightly "piano bar" streams since the pandemic began, where he takes requests from his growing audience. The evening includes a virtual tip jar, which goes to Glad Day Bookshop's emergency fund, helping artists, performers and tip-workers from the LGBTQ+ community. Check it out via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/jimclaytonjazz/). * Every Saturday, 11 a.m ET: Juno-nominated singer-songwriter Jeremy Fisher will play weekly live concerts for parents and children, running now until mid-June, via [Facebook](http://facebook.com/JeremyFisherJunior). * Tuesdays, 7 p.m. ET: Caveboy celebrates the release of its debut album with Tunesdays, where members Michelle Bensimon, Isabelle Banos and Lana Cooney break down the stories behind the songs on _Night in the Park, Kiss in the Dark_.Tune in via [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/caveboymusic/). * Daily, 2 p.m. ET: Oshawa, Ont., band Crown Lands give live music classes and host talks in their [Instagram Stories](https://www.instagram.com/crownlandsmusic/?hl=en). * Tuesdays and Thursdays, 5 p.m. ET: Toronto-based Melissa Lamm performs original songs and covers by audience request via [Twitch](https://www.twitch.tv/lammasaurus). * Saturdays, 3 p.m. AT: Coco Love Alcorn performs a weekly interactive series called Songs of Hope and Healing, via [Side Door](https://sidedooraccess.com/shows/AFWzrXKruqbr5WPrc2y2). Tickets are $7. * Sundays, 7 p.m. PT: the Meeks Duo, consisting of Scott Meek and Clare Yuan, perform from their home through[YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLrj3vUGfOeLdkVH6imuhHtbjg83W9GVJB) and [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/themeeksduo/). "We plan to do a new program every Sunday until we run out of repertoire, or until the virus gets under control, whichever comes first!" writes Meek via email. [Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CRJlTkctFvU) * Sundays until June 21: Tom Jackson hosts Almighty Voices, a digital, hour-long variety series in support of the Unison Benevolent Fund. The show will feature Susan Aglukark,Beverley Mahood, Sarah Slean,the Calgary Philharmonic Orchestra,Chantal Kreviazuk,Measha Brueggergosman and more. Watch it via YouTube and [AlmightyVoices.ca](http://almightyvoices.ca/). * Tuesdays,7:30 p.m. ET:l'Orchestre classique de Montréal will host a 45-minute session with one of the solo performers from their 2020-21 season. All performances will stream on their [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/orchestre.ca/?utm_source=Infolettre+OCM+%2F+MCO+Newsletter&utm_campaign=96cce50c52-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2020_04_06_07_19&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_14076c65d9-96cce50c52-8815065) page. * The Facebook group [Ottawa Live Music Streams!](https://www.facebook.com/groups/2628956060709220/?hc_location=ufi) has been created "to serve as a virtual venue to showcase our region's musical talent," and urged fans to get in contact with live-streaming musicians to tip them for their efforts. The page is constantly updated with both live streams and recorded performances. * Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays,8 p.m. ET:l'Orchestre symphonique de Montréal will [stream a concert from its archive](https://www.osm.ca/en/watch-and-listen-2/). "While we hit the pause button on our live shows, we will be more present than ever on our digital platforms," reads an email statement. "The OSM invites you to experience great musical moments from the comfort of your living room." * Tuesdays, 2-3 p.m.and 7:05-8 p.m. PT: Alex Maher performs Quaranstreams, a live-streaming looped performance. Half of the proceeds go to rotating charities, with the April 28 proceeds going to Mental Health Foundation of Nova Scotia. Watch via [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/alexmahermusic), [YouTube](http://youtube.com/alexmahermusic) or [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/alexmahermusic/?hl=en) * Wednesdays, 2 p.m. MT: [The Blue Jay Sessions](https://www.facebook.com/events/1073036359732892/), which normally involve Canadian musicians playing in songwriters' rounds every two months at a Calgary venue, have gone virtual — and weekly. The next session on May 27 will feature Liz, Michael Daniels, Lisa Nicole and Taylor-Rae. Tune in via [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/events/266492037824349/). (The Sessions collect donations/tips via a PayPal link and distribute evenly among the performers each week.) * After leading a successful "So Long, Marianne" sing-along from her Montreal balcony on March 22, Martha Wainwright will host the event every week with a range of other musical guests. Check out [URSA Mtl's Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/ursamtl) for dates and times each week. * [Musician Martha Wainwright invites Montrealers to another balcony singalong](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/musician-martha-wainwright-leads-another-balcony-singalong-1.5515516) * Daily, noon ET: for five to 10 minutes each day, a member of the National Arts Centre Orchestra will take to YouTube for a lunch break, which could be "anything," as NAC Orchestra music director Alexander Shelley said [via the announcement video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nyRyK3dODRY), including chatting or playing music. Check out a recent one, from May 27, below,featuring NACO violinist Manuela Milani performing Passacaglia in G Minor by baroque composer Heinrich Biber. [Video 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ITbHGhvGkU8) * Wednesdays, 7 p.m. PT: Chor Leoni Men's Choir will host a weekly live stream titled Chor Leoni Inside. According to the press release, the choir will incorporate "high-quality concert videos from the past seven years of Chor Leoni concerts, plus new video content from the choir's albums." Each live stream will also feature a musician. Watch it on [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/chorleoni/) or [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/user/chorleonimenschoir?fbclid=IwAR31LYtVvX77QZIck89NXCy3ox-gI9nrAi3u3rg7YxsWnNnYM5PxD8gykTo). ## Related Stories * [60 Years of Indigenous Music Game Changers](https://www.cbc.ca/musicinteractives/gamechangers) * [Arkells fight COVID-19 social distancing isolation with online music classes](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/arkells-music-classes-1.5500324) * [Cape Breton's Ashley MacIsaac plans online music festival during COVID-19 pandemic](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/asithappens/as-it-happens-monday-edition-1.5499097/cape-breton-s-ashley-macisaac-plans-online-music-festival-during-covid-19-pandemic-1.5499103) * [Dan Mangan played a #Quarantunes 'show to nobody' after concert postponement](https://www.cbc.ca/music/dan-mangan-played-a-quarantunes-show-to-nobody-after-concert-postponement-1.5500080) * [The Berlin Philharmonic has made its Digital Concert Hall free for everyone](https://www.cbc.ca/music/the-berlin-philharmonic-has-made-its-digital-concert-hall-free-for-everyone-1.5497260) ## Footer Links ### My Account * [Profile](https://www.cbc.ca/account/login) * [CBC Gem](https://gem.cbc.ca/benefits/) * [Newsletters](https://subscriptions.cbc.ca/listmanagement) * [About CBC Accounts](https://www.cbc.ca/account/features) ### Connect with CBC * [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/cbc/) * [X](https://x.com/cbc/) * [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/user/CBCtv) * [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/cbc/?hl=en) * [Mobile](https://cbchelp.cbc.ca/hc/en-ca/categories/115000249853-Help-with-CBC-Apps) * [RSS](https://www.cbc.ca/rss/) * [Podcasts](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/podcasts) ### Contact CBC *

state.page_text: Title: How has COVID-19 impacted Canadian musicians and fans? URL Source: https://www.cbc.ca/music/how-has-covid-19-impacted-canadian-musicians-and-fans-1.5483642 Published Time: 2020-03-03T16:42:27.253Z Markdown Content: [Skip to Main Content](https://www.cbc.ca/music/how-has-covid-19-impacted-canadian-musicians-and-fans-1.5483642#content)[Accessibility Help](https://cbchelp.cbc.ca/hc/en-ca/categories/31606111569053-Accessibility) [Menu](https://www.cbc.ca/sitemap)[CBC Gem](https://gem.cbc.ca/)[CBC Listen](https://www.cbc.ca/listen) [](https://www.cbc.ca/) Search [Search](https://www.cbc.ca/search) Sign In ##### Quick Links * [News](https://www.cbc.ca/news) * [Sports](https://www.cbc.ca/sports) * [Radio](https://www.cbc.ca/radio) * [Music](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Listen Live](https://www.cbc.ca/listen/live-radio) * [TV](https://www.cbc.ca/television) * [Watch](https://gem.cbc.ca/) * [music music](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Read](https://www.cbc.ca/music) * [Watch](https://www.cbc.ca/music/watch) * [Events](https://www.cbc.ca/music/events) * [Explore](https://www.cbc.ca/music/explore) * [Listen Live](https://www.cbc.ca/listen/live-radio) * [Junos](https://www.cbc.ca/music/junos) * [Eurovision](https://www.cbc.ca/music/eurovision) * More How has COVID-19 impacted Canadian musicians and fans? | CBC Music Loaded [Music](https://www.cbc.ca/music)·Updated # How has COVID-19 impacted Canadian musicians and fans? Céline Dion, Neil Young, Avril Lavigne and more have postponed or cancelled tour dates. ## Céline Dion, Neil Young, Avril Lavigne and more have postponed or cancelled tour dates CBC Music · Posted: Mar 03, 2020 11:42 AM EST | Last Updated: March 19, 2020 ![Image 2](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.5308013,1570134258000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C102%2C3000%2C1687%29%3B) Singer Celine Dion performs during her Courage World Tour in Quebec City on September 18.(Jacques Boissinot/THE CANADIAN PRESS) ## Social Sharing * X 0 * Reddit 0 * LinkedIn 0 * Email 0 comments As the coronavirus has been declared a pandemic by the World Health Organization —with the worldwide count of reported coronavirus cases nears 226,344, and 727 reported cases in Canada—many touring musicians are starting to rethink their international travel plans. * [Coronavirus: WHO calls COVID-19 outbreak a pandemic as Italy orders most stores to close](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/coronavirus-pandemic-1.5493411) ## **Canadian musicians who have cancelled or postponed shows so far** * Earlier this year, emo group Silverstein announced a tour to celebrate the band's 20th anniversary. That tour has now been called off and will be [rescheduled from March/April to July/August](https://exclaim.ca/music/article/silverstein_reschedule_20th_anniversary_tour_dates). * Metal musician Devin Townsend was forced to cancel his recent tour, which according to a statement "had significant financial implications" leaving him with "no idea how to make income for the next while." On March 17, Townsend launched a [GoFundMe campaign](https://www.gofundme.com/f/DevinTownsendSupportTeam?utm_medium=copy_link&utm_source=customer&utm_campaign=p_lico+share-sheet) asking fans for support to "help sustain my family whilst being able to continue working on new musical ideas." The fundraiser has already surpassed its $50,000 goal. In response, Townsend has released a new song as a thank you to those who donated. He has also promised to launch a quarantine project, which could take many forms including more music, Twitch streams and potentially a podcast. [Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k4p2g_fYwmg) * Country star Shania Twain's Let's Go!Las Vegas residency kicked off last December, but on March 16, she announced that she was rescheduling her shows due to COVID-19 concerns. "The safety and well-being of my fans, touring staff, family and anyone else who could possibly be affected is my top priority," Twain wrote on her social media accounts. * Alanis Morissette was set to take her _Jagged Little Pill_ anniversary tour to Japan, Manila, Australia and New Zealand in the coming months, but has now rescheduled those dates. "Please hang on to your tickets (except Bluesfest in Byron Bay), details to come soon for the rescheduled shows," she wrote in a Twitter post. > The safety and health of everyone comes first. Unfortunately the upcoming shows in Japan, Manila, Australia & New Zealand are being rescheduled for later dates 💔💔 please hang on to your tickets (except Bluesfest in Byron Bay), details to come soon for the rescheduled shows🙏🏼🙏🏼 > > —[@Alanis](https://twitter.com/Alanis/status/1239401811380801538) * [On March 14](https://www.instagram.com/p/B9to_hkgD3G/), electronic artist Caribou announced that all of his tour dates in March and April will be postponed. That includes shows in Canada as well as the U.S. and Europe. * Céline Dion's _Courage_ tour kicked off last September, but will be hitting pause on the rest of her North American dates from March 24 through April 27. The pop star made this announcement on March 13 via Twitter. Just two days prior, [Dion tested negative for coronavirus](https://www.eonline.com/ca/news/1130009/celine-dion-tests-negative-for-coronavirus-after-common-cold-symptoms)after coming down with a cold, but postponed two tour dates. > Céline Dion #CourageWorldTour dates postponed in North America. Show dates from March 24 through April 27, 2020 to be rescheduled. - Team Célinehttps://t.co/s2dzxpp9mepic.twitter.com/9h2qFGxYxY > > —[@celinedion](https://twitter.com/celinedion/status/1238269514644697088) * Singer-songwriter Sarah Harmer was scheduled to kick off her Canadian tour to support her latest album,_Are You Gone_, in Peterborough, Ont., on March 24. But on March 13, Harmer decided to reschedule her spring shows "to a time in the hopefully near future when the threat of the COVID-19 virus has passed," she wrote in an [online post](https://www.facebook.com/sarahharmermusic/photos/a.10158902309729128/10159376175324128/?type=3&theater). * On March 11, Tegan and Sara announced their 2020 Tonight We're Seeing Colors tour, which would have the Canadian pop group on the road from May through September. The next day, they released a followup message not postponing the shows, but postponing any ticket sales. "We'll keep you updated and hope that all of you are being careful and safe," they wrote in a [Twitter post](https://twitter.com/teganandsara/status/1238202649486360576). > Hi everybody! We're going to postpone our ticket on-sale until we have a clearer picture of how to proceed with the COVID-19 situation in the USA and Canada. We'll keep you updated and hope that all of you are being careful and safe. xo, T&S pic.twitter.com/XyfpdpJJ6R > > —[@teganandsara](https://twitter.com/teganandsara/status/1238202649486360576) * Oakville, Ontario-born, Los Angeles-based pop musician Allie X has also postponed her North American tour. In a Twitter post, she told fans: "Please wait for me. I am working on rescheduling these dates and am looking forward to rejoicing, crying, dancing, screaming and laughing with you." > 😔 I’m sorry. I love you ❤️ we’ll get through this and do this tour as soon as possible. pic.twitter.com/vJ4sJqs7dd > > —[@alliex](https://twitter.com/alliex/status/1238514063061073921) * _Schitt's Creek_ star and musician Noah Reid was in the middle of his First Time Out tour, but will be postponing and rescheduling the remainder of his March shows in the U.S. In a press release, Reid said "it feels like the right thing to do." * 2020 Juno-nominated act the Glorious Sons are halting their cross-Canada tour. They were also scheduled to perform at the Juno Awards, [which announced its cancellation on March 12](http://www.cbc.ca/music/junos/news/2020-juno-awards-cancelled-over-coronavirus-concerns-1.5494991). * Also on March 12, Michael Bublé took to Twitter to postpone the start of his U.S. tour, pushing shows that would've run from March 17 to April 5. New dates, he added, will be "announced shortly." > Michael's run of US tour dates beginning March 17th through April 5th have been postponed, with new dates in the same markets to be announced shortly. Tickets will be honored for the rescheduled shows. pic.twitter.com/VImYY4Co9r > > —[@MichaelBuble](https://twitter.com/MichaelBuble/status/1238157710027153408) * That same day, Ben Cook, member of Toronto hardcore band F--ked Up and leader of his own side project, Young Guv, set up a [GoFundMe fundraiser](https://www.gofundme.com/f/helptheguvband?utm_medium=social&utm_source=facebook&utm_campaign=p_na+share-sheet&rcid=865e266a60e14803a9c23b4fedeb87ed&fbclid=IwAR1Ip1FQOgZSVCcYUTfpeWhzCFyZq3ZyW4PQfKNqygw1_qRihHYtp3YSc2s) to help him, his Young Guv bandmates and their driver return to their respective homes in New York and Canada following the cancellation of their tour with Kentucky rock band White Reaper. "We were depending on this tour to pay our way through our travels," Cook wrote. "The mounting costs related to touring, gas, accommodations, and musician's fees have driven me deep into the red financially. To make things worse, I, along with every member of my band, currently have no place to go, as we have all sublet our rooms for the month of March." The campaign has now reached its $5,000 goal, less than a day after launching it. * On March 7, Neil Young took to his [NYA Times-Contrarian website](https://neilyoungarchives.com/news/1/article?id=Message-From-Neil-Uncertain-Times) to address the status of his long-awaited tour with his band, Crazy Horse. "The idea of announcing the tour and putting tickets on sale is questionable and needs to be thought through," he wrote. "We're all super ready to go, and the last thing we want to do is put people at risk, especially our older audience. No one wants to become sick in this pandemic." Young ended his note by sending his best wishes to "all of the health care and government workers in all of the world, to all the scientists who will learn and share with us the best ways to ensure survival in our world challenged." * Concert pianist Angela Hewitt, who's based in England but performs around the world, announced on March 5 that her recitals in Milan and Florence this month were cancelled by government decree. For now, her annual [Trasimeno Music Festival](https://www.cbc.ca/music/why-this-is-the-year-to-cross-angela-hewitt-s-umbrian-music-festival-off-your-bucket-list-1.5150044) in Italy's Umbria region is still going ahead, but she's got concerns. "The financial responsibility for the festival falls on my own shoulders," [she posted on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=2822587201164308&id=201013549988366), "and I simply cannot risk losing a lot of money over it and I (and my staff) can't put in the huge amount of work and emotional involvement, only to have it all fall apart at the last moment. We depend on our audience who travel from all over the world, and at the moment that's not happening." * The National Youth Orchestra of Canada cancelled its upcoming concert tour to Germany, Slovenia and Croatia [over concerns of the potential spread of coronavirus](https://www.facebook.com/nyoconjc/posts/10157266231457169:0). * Canadian pop star Avril Lavigne was set to kick off the Asia leg of her world tour in Shenzhen, China, on April 23, but the singer has now cancelled that string of shows as well as her Europe leg due to concerns over the continued coronavirus outbreak. "I am so sad to announce that we are unable to tour the Asian markets," Lavigne told fans in a social media post. "Please everybody take care of yourselves and stay healthy. You're in my thoughts and prayers and we are hoping to announce rescheduled shows soon." * Montreal rock band Wolf Parade also posted a message online earlier this week informing fans that it would not move forward with its European tour. "We feel strongly that it would be both globally irresponsible and potentially risky for the band to carry out the tour at this time," the band wrote. "The amount of major airports, international driving, and crowds of people we would be interacting with —they all combine to form what is ultimately a bad idea; a recipe for a potential worst-case-scenario in which we could end up being unknown carriers of the virus across multiple borders, or end up ill and/or quarantine ourselves overseas." The band members assured fans that they are in the middle of rescheduling their shows, but since those aren't set yet fans should"get a refund for the cancelled dates now." > pic.twitter.com/tC6KkoWxGa > > —[@WolfParade](https://twitter.com/WolfParade/status/1234526776447008768) * Singer-songwriter Mac DeMarco has not publicly released a statement but has cancelled his upcoming Japan tour (including dates in Sapporo, Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka, Hiroshima and Fukuoka), which was originally scheduled for April. * [K-pop stars BTS cancel Seoul kick-off of world tour over coronavirus](https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/bts-virus-cancellations-1.5476453) * [Spreading coronavirus affects BTS shows, halts Mission: Impossible shoot](https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/coronavirus-entertainment-world-1.5474987) Internationally, the coronavirus has affected a number of other touring musicians including K-pop stars BTS, rock groups Green Day and Jimmy Eat World, U.K. rapper Stormzy, R&B artist Khalid and English rockers New Order. ## **Big festivals and events that are following suit** * On March 17, the East Coast Music Awards, which were to take place April 29 to May 3 in St. John's,announced the cancellation of its 2020 festival and conference due to concerns about COVID-19. In a [statement](https://ymlp.com/zjUCk9?fbclid=IwAR0nklGRFVLdccvCkvII18xL-3EjNFOzdBPwdJ5-RqFSzfzRK38iVFTHDUQ), the ECMA board of directors wrote: "In the coming weeks and months, the ECMA will explore alternative ways to celebrate the accomplishments of our world-class regional talent and honour the winners of the 2020 East Coast Music Awards." * Toronto's Canadian Music Week was scheduled to take place from May 19 to 23, but has now been moved to September 8 to 13, according to a [statement](https://nowtoronto.com/music/canadian-music-week-cmw-2020-postponed/) released on March 16. All badges and wristbands will be honoured for the new dates. * The 2020 SOCAN Awards were cancelled after Ontario's chief medical officer issued instructions to suspend gatherings of more than 250 people. It was originally scheduled to take place on March 30 in Toronto. * Record Store Day 2020, a global music event where limited edition releases are made available at local record stores, has been moved from April 18 to June 20. In a [statement](https://recordstoreday.com/NewsItem/9003), its organizers said, "RSD acknowledges the need to be good citizens of both the local and worldwide communities while still giving our participating stores around the world the best chance to have a profitable, successful Record Store Day." This year includes special releases from Mac DeMarco, k.d. lang, the Dead South and Tegan and Sara. * In Toronto, concert venues Roy Thomson Hall and Massey Hall have suspended all events for the next two weeks. * On March 12, FACTOR, a non-profit organization that provides funding for Canadian musicians and recording projects, announced that it would honour "all approved commitments at 100 per cent of the amount approved for funding in situations where the event or activity was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic," [according to a statement on its website](https://www.factor.ca/covid-19-update-cancellation-policy/). The statement singles out the South by Southwest and Juno Award cancellations specifically, as well as "all other activities such as tours, showcases and certain collective events." * The city of Austin declared a "local disaster" on March 7 due to the spread of COVID-19, effectively [cancelling the music, film and tech conference South by Southwest](https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/entertainment-cancellations-coronavirus-1.5488328). Thousands of musical acts normally descend upon the capital of Texas to perform each March (March 16-22 this time around), and this year Canadian acts like Basia Bulat, Haviah Mighty, Dan Mangan, Snotty Nose Rez Kids and plenty more find themselves without showcases. The Canadian organization Side Door, which was co-founded by Mangan and Laura Simpson and matches artists with hosts (often house concerts) via [sidedooraccess.com](https://sidedooraccess.com/site/founders), had organized a South by Southwest-specific tour route, with Canadian and American artists making their way to Austin by playing small-venue shows on their drive down. Some of those artists are going to continue to play select dates, including Ontario band Whoop-Szo, though Polaris Prize shortlister Partner is no longer on the list. (You can get a full update on that tour [here](https://sidedooraccess.com/site/side-door-to-sxsw?fbclid=IwAR27ZAdeWGngBfRPNmaaYi5PCaKo7fdtwPME5wdrU4jcOBBZ5SBwzkWUtCA).) * Ottawa's RBC Bluesfest has yet to cancel, but is instead "closely monitoring the situation and will carefully follow the recommendation of public health experts," according to a [statement](https://ottawabluesfest.ca/march10_2020_covid-19_update/?fbclid=IwAR2Hdw9KYEAJ4LHoIAtGYOTolPtVMzr5nG3vg7d688vcMySfQ7SQIjsbUUU). Unlike many of the events that have been pushed, Bluesfest is slated later in the summer, taking place from July 9 to 19. ## Related Stories * [Arctic Winter Games 'in good shape' with COVID-19 precautions](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/awg-2020-covid-19-whitehorse-1.5483188) * [All about Avril Lavigne: how the teenaged pop-punk poet changed everything](https://www.cbc.ca/music/all-about-avril-lavigne-how-the-teenaged-pop-punk-poet-changed-everything-1.5035556) * [The 10 most iconic Rolling Stone covers featuring Canadian musicians](https://www.cbc.ca/music/the-10-most-iconic-rolling-stone-covers-featuring-canadian-musicians-1.5351994) ## Comments **Comments are typically open between 6 a.m. and 11:30 p.m. ET.** Comments may be unavailable based on different considerations, including moderation capacity, the type of moderation needed, and legal concerns. To encourage thoughtful and respectful conversations, full names will appear with each submission to CBC's online communities. CBC does not endorse the opinions expressed in comments. # More Free Music!

[March 18, 2020](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/18/more-free-music/ "3:09 pm") by [Chris Gallant](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/author/catapultingintoclassical/ "View all posts by Chris Gallant")[2 Comments](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/2020/03/18/more-free-music/#comments)

[![Image 2: Broadcast tower topped by music note, globe in background](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/broadcast-tower-with-globe002.jpg?w=140&h=200)](https://catapultingintoclassical.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/broadcast-tower-with-globe002.jpg)

The ranks of musical institutions and performers helping us all get through the current health crisis together are growing. Here’s are my latest finds.

The Detroit Symphony Orchestra has now made its Replay archive of past concerts available for free. Enjoy high-definition recordings with fantastic sound in the comfort of your own home. Visit [https://livefromorchestrahall.vhx.tv/browse](https://livefromorchestrahall.vhx.tv/browse) to access the performances. There, you can set up a free account, but it is not mandatory. You can search the offerings by composer or time period.

Piano fans! Igor Levit is giving nightly live “House Concerts” on Twitter ([twitter.com/igorpianist](https://twitter.com/igorpianist)). See his Twitter feed for times and for other performances. Boris Giltburg ([https://twitter.com/BorisGiltburg](https://twitter.com/BorisGiltburg)) will also be offering Twitter performances. [Added note: you don’t need a twitter account to see the concerts].

You also might want to check out the YouTube channel of [Wigmore Hall](https://www.youtube.com/user/wigmorehall), especially their Beethoven 250 Festival recordings.

Opera fans! The Teatro Regio in Turin is offering [#operaonthesofa](https://www.teatroregio.torino.it/en/news/operaonthesofa). Check out their website for details, or go to their [YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLhaJamV0Nxm8nTJjWKOKI1C26pEPQC2wt) to check out the playlist. The [Vienna State Opera](http://www.staatsoperlive.com/) is also opening their archive of performances. To see the archive, you will need to set up a free account. They are also livestreaming a different performance each night. Livestreams begin at 17:00 or 19:00 CET (GMT +1), and those are available for 24 hours.

Also, check out WKAR’s schedule of livestream performances. You can find it at [https://www.wkar.org/post/list-live-streaming-concerts#stream/0](https://www.wkar.org/post/list-live-streaming-concerts#stream/0).

Off topic, but if you need some calm, and something a little different, I’d like to suggest the live cams at the [Monterey Bay Aquarium](https://www.montereybayaquarium.org/animals/live-cams) or the [National Aquarium](https://www.aqua.org/Experience/live). You can watch fish, penguins, birds, jellyfish (oddly mesmerizing—nature’s lava lamp), or just the beautiful bay. You can find a wide variety of animals and natural scenery on livecam at [explore.org](https://explore.org/livecams) (I particularly recommend the [Zen Cams](https://explore.org/livecams/zen-den/)). Add your own classical soundtrack if you’d like! Nature endures; spring is coming.
