*   [Collections](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/#browse-collections)
*   [About](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/about)
*   [Explore](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/search)

## About Bay Area Radio Museum and Hall of Fame

[The Bay Area Radio Museum and Hall of Fame](http://bayarearadio.org/) (BARHOF) presents archival broadcasts, historical documents, photos, music surveys and biographies that tell the story of Bay Area radio. BARHOF is a program of the [California Historical Radio Society](http://https//californiahistoricalradio.com), a 501(c)(3) non-profit educational organization based in Alameda, CA. Our exhibits on DIVA are drawn from thousands of hours of recordings of Bay Area radio broadcasts held in our collection. ([more](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/about))

Total number of items 49 Total number of views 1,412

## Collections

[](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12729)

#### [Bay Area Radio Commercials](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12729)

 Radio commercials held in the archives of the Bay Area Radio Museum and Hall of Fame tell the story of Bay Area life through the years. 

[](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12731)

#### [Radio Classics](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12731)

 Examples of broadcasts showing the rich history of radio creativity in the Bay Area. 

[](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12733)

#### [Bay Area Radio Hall of Fame Inductees](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12733)

 Examples of the work of members of the Bay Area Radio Hall of Fame (BARHOF). 

[](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12732)

#### [The Mal Sharpe Collection](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12732)

 Mal Sharpe (1936-2020) was a memorable radio performer. His Bay Area career began with the Coyle and Sharpe show on KGO in the early 1960s and evolved into years of unique commercials in which he perfected an "on the street" interview style. 

[](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12730)

#### [Sheila Rene Backstage](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/barm/12730)

 Sheila Rene Backstage was the work of pioneering rock interviewer Sheila Rene. These programs aired in 1981 and 1982 on KSJO, KSFX, and a handful of other FM stations. 

## Contact

 Questions or comments about our exhibits? Please email us at: help@bayarearadio.org 

### DIVA @ Academic Technology

DIVA is a project of Academic Technology at [San Francisco State University](http://www.sfsu.edu/).

For additional information about DIVA please visit our [FAQ page](https://at.sfsu.edu/diva).  Contact us at [digitize@sfsu.edu](mailto:digitize@sfsu.edu)

## About Poetry Center Digital Archive

[The Poetry Center](http://poetry.sfsu.edu/)'s dedicated online archive makes available new video recordings (with audio downloads), plus early audio recordings from the 1950s onward. Digital documents are sourced from unique magnetic-tape recordings, housed on-site in The Poetry Center's American Poetry Archives collection at San Francisco State University. Near all recordings document the Poetry Center Reading Series. New recordings are added as programs occur each season, Fall and Spring. Historic recordings are added as digital files are prepared and cataloged. ([more](https://diva.sfsu.edu/collections/collections/poetrycenter/about))

An eclectic mix of sponsored videos and curated performances for your viewing pleasure. Have a video to promote? We'll feature it here. [Learn how](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/about-video-of-the-day).

### [Everything in its Right Place](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-everything-in-its-right-place "View \"Everything in its Right Place\" jazz video")

Peter Martin  
Duration: 04:53   
320 views

Radiohead’s track “Everything in its Right Place” was seminal. It announced the transition of the band from indie guitar rock to ambient pulse music. The song, from 2000, has since been covered by several stars, including [Robert Glasper](javascript:void(0)) and [Brad Mehldau](javascript:void(0)), but for the best version when it comes to a polished video, here’s a vote for the version from Open Studio. Open Studio is an online jazz teaching platform covering beginner to master class levels. Among its well-known teachers are the performers on this track: [Peter Martin](javascript:void(0)) on piano, [Adam Maness](javascript:void(0)) on synthesizer, [Bob DeBoo](javascript:void(0)) on bass and bass synthesizer, and [Kaleb Kirby](javascript:void(0)) on drums. Completed in a single take, this Radiohead cover tune offers an experience that should get any jazz fan’s head bobbing. Especially worth noting are the laid-back intensity; the dark visual backdrop contrasted with angled spotlights; the clever knob-turning effect from muffled tone to bright at 00:36; the reharmonized piano solo at 1:34, and the set-'em-loose drum solo.

### [Defying Gravity](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-defying-gravity "View \"Defying Gravity\" jazz video")

Amanda Barise  
Duration: 04:05   
246 views

Powerhouse collective, Third Reprise, breathes electric, new life into theater standards by reimagining them through a sophisticated jazz-funk lens. Fronted on this tune by the soulful, soaring vocals of Amanda Barise and anchored by arranger Daniel Rudin's sharp instrumentation, this live studio performance transforms a Broadway classic, “Defying Gravity,” from the musical and movie _Wicked_, into an absolute groove monster. Listen for the exceptionally tight horn-driven syncopation, the slick synth textures, and a blistering bassline that underpins Barise's vocal acrobatics during the climax. It takes (show/jazz/funk) fusion in a whole new direction.

Every day is a good day to “Take the 'A' Train.” That’s especially true when one encounters a highly-talented, yet lesser-known gypsy jazz band driving the train’s wheels at 134 beats per minute. Guitarists [Clement Reboul](javascript:void(0)) and Aurélien Robert, upright bassist Ghali Hadefi and guest clarinetist Hugo Proy nail the tempo and hot jazz feel, and the guitarists perfectly complement each others’ strumming and riffs. The coordination is a sign of the years of experience that the collective Clément Reboul’s Jazz Manouche has working together. All aboard!

### [Stolen Moments](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-stolen-moments "View \"Stolen Moments\" jazz video")

Lee Ritenour  
Duration: 7:20   
234 views

Can any song put you in a melancholy mood better than “Stolen Moments,” composed by [Oliver Nelson](javascript:void(0)) with its major release in 1961? Well, there’s a case to be made for another version of the song to be considered the smokiest and most swinging -- it’s the all-star group featuring [Lee Ritenour](javascript:void(0)) (guitar), [Ernie Watts](javascript:void(0)) (tenor sax), [Alan Broadbent](javascript:void(0)) (piano), plus [Harvey Mason](javascript:void(0)) (drums) and [Brian Bromberg](javascript:void(0)) (bass). This 1990 live version is a master class on how to play with elastic time and how to build a solo from the ground up. In particular, Broadbent opens with a melange of extended harmonies; Ritenour follows with his best impression of [Wes Montgomery](javascript:void(0))’s octave double-stops, and finally Watts provides the coup de grace with a burning, emotional solo. By the way, the [New York Voices](javascript:void(0)) version on Youtube is really good, too. What’s your favorite “Stolen Moments?"

### [Cassandra Wilson at North Sea Jazz](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-cassandra-wilson-at-north-sea-jazz "View \"Cassandra Wilson at North Sea Jazz\" jazz video")

Cassandra Wilson  
Duration: 65:15   
518 views

Cassandra Wilson was a singular voice in the world of jazz. A smoky contralto, she poured a well of emotion into everything she sang — her blues ached, her ballads floated, her percussion-driven grooves felt visceral. She skillfully reinvented arrangements from the canon of jazz standards, pop, blues, folk and African music. What never changed was the space she left around the phrases, room enough for every listener in the room to pour in their own meaning. Wilson’s accomplishments led her to be named “America’s Best Singer” in 2001 by Time Magazine and to be bestowed a National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Master award in 2022. The full range of the songstress was well-captured at the North Sea Jazz Festival in 2003, especially on “Lay, Lady, Lay” (by [Bob Dylan](javascript:void(0))) at 2:08, “I Want More” at 34:20, and “Tupelo Honey” (by [Van Morrison](javascript:void(0))) at 40:00. Cassandra Wilson passed away September 1, 2026.

### [Curves Ahead](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-curves-ahead "View \"Curves Ahead\" jazz video")

Duration: 5:26   
216 views

Starting in the 1980s, smooth jazz greatly expanded the audience for jazz-adjacent music. The best performers of this sub-genre could solo ably enough to please casual listeners. However, the Achilles Heel of the smooth movement was that the typical song’s melody and changes weren’t unique and catchy enough to warrant a passionate devotion. Without that, the tunes could border on elevator “muzak.” The Rippingtons, led by guitarist Russ Freeman, met and surpassed that melodic hurdle with contemporary jazz hits such as “Welcome to the St. James’ Club,” “Tourist in Paradise” and “Curves Ahead." The band’s doubled-up leads on guitar (or guitar synth penny whistle) and sax, phat synth sounds, and locked-in digital and acoustic percussion rhythms were easy to identify on the radio. Also, be sure to listen for the poppin' bass riffs. The Rippingtons join [Spyro Gyra](javascript:void(0)), [Fattburger](javascript:void(0)) and [Fourplay](javascript:void(0)) among the most satisfying groups of that era.

### [What U Won't Do 4 Love](https://www.allaboutjazz.com/media/video-what-u-wont-do-4-love "View \"What U Won't Do 4 Love\" jazz video")

Tony Adamo  
Duration: 3:28   
706 views

"What U Won't Do 4 Love" by Tony Adamo is a refreshing, soulful masterclass in modern jazz-funk fusion. Released in mid-2026 on Saint Jaz Records, the track serves as a groovy, geography-spanning love letter that bridges classic urban soundscapes with Adamo's signature hipster flair. Instead of leaning purely into his iconic, rapid-fire spoken-word “sing- speak," Adamo opts for a deeply melodic, soulful vocal delivery that mirrors the warmth of 1970s R&B.   
  
 The lyrics depart from Adamo's usual inside-jazz-history references to deliver a rhythmic, multi-city travelogue centered on devotion. Adamo charts a musical map across America's greatest sonic hubs—shouting out the “Motor City" (Detroit), Philly, the “Big Apple" (New York), “Shy Town" (Chicago), Miami, Atlanta, Raleigh, and Oakland—before steering the track right back home to a “city by the Bay" (San Francisco). The songwriting cleverly uses travel and navigation imagery ("love map," “compass," “lighthouse") to frame a story about a wandering mind finally finding anchor in true love.   
  
 Vocal Performance: 4.5/5 – Deeply earnest, smooth, and an excellent display of Adamo's pure singing range. Instrumentation: 5/5 – A premium, locked-in rhythm section that keeps your feet moving from start to finish. Atmosphere: 4.8/5 – Funky, nostalgic, yet thoroughly modern and accessible to both jazz purists and mainstream R&B fans.   
  
 ~Ben Price, Underground Jazz/The UK

# South Bend Symphony, local arts groups to collaborate for online concert

Tribune Staff Report

South Bend Tribune

Dec. 7, 2020, 6:00 a.m. ET

[](link_12)[](link_13)[](mailto:?subject=South%20Bend%20Symphony%2C%20local%20arts%20groups%20to%20collaborate%20for%20online%20concert%20-%20from%20South%20Bend%20Tribune&body=South%20Bend%20Symphony%2C%20local%20arts%20groups%20to%20collaborate%20for%20online%20concert%0A%0ASOUTH%20BEND%20%E2%80%94%20The%20South%20Bend%20Symphony%20Orchestra%2C%20South%20Bend%20Civic%20Theatre%20and%20other%20local%20performing%20arts%20groups%20are%20collaborating%20on%20an%20online%20holiday%20concert%20to%20premiere%20at%207%20p.m.%20Dec.%2019%2C%20at%20southbendsymphony.org%2FLOC%20and%20sbct.org%2FLOC.%0A%0ACheck%20out%20this%20story%20on%20southbendtribune.com%3A%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.southbendtribune.com%2Fstory%2Fentertainment%2Fmusic%2F2020%2F12%2F07%2Fsouth-bend-symphony-local-arts-groups-to-collaborate-for-online-conce%2F116062114%2F)

[Video 1](https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/entertainment/music/2020/12/07/south-bend-symphony-local-arts-groups-to-collaborate-for-online-conce/116062114/)

SOUTH BEND — The South Bend Symphony Orchestra, South Bend Civic Theatre and other local performing arts groups are collaborating on an online holiday concert to premiere at 7 p.m. Dec. 19, at southbendsymphony.org/LOC and sbct.org/LOC.

Titled “Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration,” it explores the traditions of five cultural groups — Jewish, African American, Pokagon Band of Potawatomi, Latinx and Eastern Orthodox — through dance, storytelling and symphonic music.

As part of the video presentation, the public is invited to submit videos of themselves and loved ones holding a single candle. Video submissions should be 5-7 seconds in length, with no audio, and are due by Saturday at sbct.org/candlevideo.

After the video premieres, it will be available to the public until Jan. 6.

# PRESENTED BY THE SOUTH BEND SYMPHONY ORCHESTRA AND SOUTH BEND CIVIC THEATRE

Will you Light One Candle for our holiday celebration?

## VIDEO SUBMISSION REQUEST

Share a video clip to be included in our upcoming holiday concert!

[Submit your video](link_24)

![Image 3: SBSO_LockUp_Reverse](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/SBSO_LockUp_Reverse-300x256.png)

## How to participate

The South Bend Symphony Orchestra and South Bend Civic Theatre are seeking video submissions for their upcoming holiday concert. Will you share your light? Your video will be featured during the upcoming _Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration._



#### Record your video

Film a video of yourself (alone or with loved ones) holding a single candle. Videos should be no longer than 5-7 seconds consider it a “moving image.”



#### SUBMIT YOUR FILE

Upload your file no later than Dec. 12 using our [online form](link_24). If you have trouble, reach out to marketing@sbct.org.



#### TUNE IN ON DEC. 19

Set a reminder for 7 p.m. Dec. 19 when we premiere _Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration._ Sign up below to receive a reminder!

## Sign up for Light One Candle updates!

Sign up for our email list to receive updates from the South Bend Symphony Orchestra and the South Bend Civic Theatre about the free _Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration!_

# Author: Jennifer Melick

Jennifer Melick, _Symphony_ magazine’s former longtime managing editor, is a freelance journalist based in Detroit.

## [New home under construction for LA Phil’s YOLA inspires hope for systemic change in classical field](link_8)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_8)

![Image 2](https://live-hub-american-orchestras.pantheonsite.io/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/YOLA-students-USE-THIS-800x400-.png)
Young musicians in the Los Angeles Philharmonic’s Youth Orchestra Los Angeles (YOLA).

“Last month, architect Frank Gehry and Los Angeles Philharmonic CEO Chad Smith gave me a masked hard-hat tour of the nearly finished Judith and Thomas L. Beckmen YOLA Center at Inglewood,” writes Mark Swed in Thursday’s (12/10) [_Los Angeles Times_](link_10). “Gehry’s reimagining of an abandoned bank building … the YOLA Center [is] intended to serve music students from Inglewood and surrounding communities [as a home for] Youth Orchestra Los Angeles … Gustavo Dudamel’s educational initiative begun in 2007…. When it is up and running… you will see young musicians from the community rehearsing or performing … in an airy, light-filled, sophisticated, gorgeous state-of-the-art building … Orchestras … have the imperative of creating an innovative online presence to hold onto patrons … all while taking on new and timely repertory, particularly that of composers of color…. For real systemic change, we need a real system in place, something solid and lasting. YOLA is that system. It trains talent and attracts audiences…. It generates enthusiasm, broadens horizons and inspires commitment…. There are YOLA grads to prove it attending college and working for the L.A. Phil. Someday in the not distant future, grads will be playing in the orchestra.”

## [South Bend Symphony and area arts groups partner for multicultural online holiday concert](link_11)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_11)
The South Bend Symphony Orchestra is collaborating with the South Bend Civic Theatre and other area performing arts groups to produce an online holiday concert, set to premiere on Dec. 19 at the South Bend Symphony and South Bend City Theatre websites. The video presentation, “Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration,” will explore traditions of five cultural groups—Jewish, African American, Pokagon Band of Potawatomi, Latinx and Eastern Orthodox—through dance, storytelling, and symphonic music. The public is invited to submit videos of themselves and loved ones holding a single candle to be included in the video presentation. Video submissions should be five to seven seconds in length, with no audio, and are due by December 12 at [sbct.org/candlevideo](link_12). The holiday video will remain posted until January 6.

## [Australia’s Adelaide Symphony to spotlight women composers in redesigned 2021 season](link_13)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_13)
“The Adelaide Symphony Orchestra has unveiled the first half of its 2021 season, spanning February to July … as well as announcing a new initiative to … support the development of female composers,” writes Angus McPherson in Sunday’s (12/6) [_Limelight Magazine_](link_14) (Australia).“Each of the mainstage [concerts will] include at least one work written by a woman. The first concert for the year will open with Elena Kats-Chernin’s _Big Rhap_, alongside Samuel Barber’s Knoxville: Summer of 1915 … and Tchaikovsky’s Symphony No 4…. April will see Lili Boulanger’s _D’un matin de Printemps_, [and] Myriam Hyde’s _An Adelaide Overture_ opens a [July] concert…. A special event in June … curated by composer Anne Cawrse, will exclusively feature music written by … women composers…. ‘One of the many devastating impacts of COVID-19 was that it completely unpicked what was a very impressive 2020 line-up of women conductors: Jessica Gethin, Elim Chan, Gemma New, Elena Schwarz,’ Managing Director Vincent Ciccarello said…. The 2021 season will also feature a new Meditation Series (with music from Peggy Glanville-Hicks to Arvo Pärt, and featuring a world premiere by Luke Altmann)…. The ASO’s Adelaide Festival collaborations also include … the world premiere of a new concerto by Nigel Westlake for two guitars.”

## [Teaching “Nutcracker” remotely, to visually impaired dance and music students](link_15)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_15)
“On a November afternoon, seven young students twirled, hopped and lifted their chests to the sky, as Waltz of the Snowflakes from ‘The Nutcracker’ played through their computer speakers,” writes Siobhan Burke in Sunday’s (12/6) [_New York Times_](link_16). “Gathered for a weekly Zoom class, they had arrived at a part of the lesson that one of their teachers, Jenny Seham, called ‘freestyle snow dancing.’ … Listening is a fundamental skill for anyone learning to dance, but especially so for Ms. Seham’s students. As a longtime teaching artist with National Dance Institute, which brings dance education to New York City children, Ms. Seham has worked for over a decade with students who are blind and visually impaired, in partnership with the Filomen M. D’Agostino Greenberg Music School. This year, for the first time, the music school—which serves students of all ages with vision loss—is offering a five-week ‘Nutcracker’ appreciation course to bring to life the holiday classic in a multisensory way…. Matthew Herrera, 12, … who is visually impaired … said that as a musician who studies piano and voice, improvising is one of his strengths—and the same goes for dance…. ‘It’s a beautiful thing.’ ”

## [Central Florida nonprofits work to increase arts opportunities for people of color](link_17)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_17)
“Across the Central Florida cultural scene … efforts to increase inclusion of nonwhite performers, leaders and programming require money—money that is hard to come by,” writes Matthew J. Palm in Sunday’s (12/6) [_Orlando Sentinel_](link_18) (FL). “Help may be on the way. ‘We’d like to provide opportunities for people of color to learn and grow, because you don’t see people of color in administration, in leadership roles,’ said Crystal Priester, director of development at United Arts of Central Florida…. One way will be through a new program providing financial support to organizations led by and creating events for people of color….. Also seeking to open doors is a new Orange County committee for Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, launched in September…. Options include requiring organizations to demonstrate inclusivity before receiving grants … or even asking county commissioners to create a new fund specifically for inclusion initiatives…. In the latest … grants … organizations such as the Orlando Philharmonic Orchestra, Orlando Shakes, Orlando Repertory Theatre and Central Florida Community Arts received funding for various training and marketing efforts…. As the economic fallout from the coronavirus pandemic continues, corporate sponsorship may be harder to find. But at United Arts, Priester said she’ll keep looking.”

## [Opinion: There can be no economic recovery without an arts recovery](link_19)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_19)
“The recent decision by Salt Lake County to temporarily close its performing arts venues came as a tough blow to the arts industry,” writes Keith Carrick, the Utah Symphony’s principal percussionist, in Sunday’s (12/6) [_Salt Lake Tribune_](link_20) (UT). “The pandemic continues to be a grueling experience for so many of our businesses that depend on the revenue they would receive during the Christmas season. Our performing arts institutions are certainly no different…. At some point in the future, it will be necessary to enact an economic recovery plan, and there can be no economic recovery without an arts recovery.… Our performing arts institutions are an integral part of the economic ecosystem, having a $300 million annual economic impact in Salt Lake City alone, and supporting 40,000 jobs statewide…. Musicians, actors and dancers will play an essential role in the emotional healing and celebration that will take place when we can safely congregate again…. One thought—assuming it’s safe, why not plan a weeklong celebration over the summer to visit together again, see shows, eat out and shop? It may be just the jump-start businesses and institutions will need coming out of the pandemic. Perhaps, Christmas in July?”

## [Philadelphia Orchestra names Nathalie Stutzmann as principal guest conductor, announces additional virtual concerts](link_21)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_21)
“The Philadelphia Orchestra has mapped out its virtual concerts through the end of the season—and added a major new voice to its artistic team,” writes Peter Dobrin in Tuesday’s (12/8) [_Philadelphia Inquirer_](link_22). “Nathalie Stutzmann, the much-loved French contralto and conductor, will take up the post of principal guest conductor.… She expects to conduct about three weeks each year in the main subscription series, plus additional concerts.… Stutzmann starts her three-year deal beginning with the 2021-22 season…. The orchestra on Tuesday also announced details of more than a dozen new online productions between January and June, one streaming about every two weeks…. Among the highlights of the rest of the pandemic-altered season are the first concerto appearance with the orchestra by new principal oboist Philippe Tondre, a collaboration with Brian Sanders’ JUNK dance troupe, and the May performance of _Vigil_ in tribute to Breonna Taylor. Audiences will also hear the Philadelphia Orchestra’s first performances of Florence Price’s Piano Concerto in One Movement, Gershwin’s original jazz band version of _Rhapsody in Blue_, and Mahler’s _Das Lied von der Erde_ in a chamber orchestra reduction.… Additional concerts this season …are likely to fall into place at a later date.”

## [Oklahoma City Philharmonic’s holiday show goes virtual; January concerts postponed](link_23)

Posted on December 9, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_23)

![Image 3](https://live-hub-american-orchestras.pantheonsite.io/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/800x400-Alexander-Mickelthwate-conducts-OKC-Phil-Oct-2020-credit-Heather-Hanson.jpg)
Music Director Alexander Mickelthwate conducts the Oklahoma City Philharmonic in October 2020. Photo by Heather Hanson

“After planning to replace its annual holiday extravaganza ‘The Christmas Show’ with a stripped-down, socially distanced ‘A Classic Christmas,’ the Oklahoma City Philharmonic announced just before Thanksgiving new plans to make this year’s yuletide concert a streaming-only event,” due to rising COVID-19 infection rates, writes Brandy McDonnell in Friday’s (12/4) [_Daily Oklahoman_](link_24) (Oklahoma City). “ ‘It’s going to be very innovative—and I think it’s going to be good,’ said Susan Webb, the OKC Philharmonic’s marketing director…. ‘It will be only with two soloists … not the big staging, not the big choirs and everything,’ said Music Director Alexander Mickelthwate … The orchestra has been performing the Christmas numbers this week, with Spark Creative CEO Christopher Lloyd, a former OKC Philharmonic associate board member, directing the videography. The digital concert is slated to debut Sunday [and] will be available for unlimited viewing through Christmas Day…. The OKC Philharmonic also has postponed its entire January performance slate … with new dates to be announced next month. ‘We are striving to be nimble in fulfilling our mission to the community, which is to bring inspiration and joy through orchestral music,’ said Executive Director Agnieszka Rakhmatullaev in a statement.”

## [Wheeling Symphony’s virtual premiere of Primiani’s “Gaudete for Orchestra”](link_25)

Posted on December 7, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_25)
On December 10 at 7 p.m. ET, the Wheeling Symphony Orchestra will launch the world premiere of Leanna Primiani’s _Gaudete for Orchestra_, performed on WTRF-CBS and on WTRF.com. The seven-minute work is “based on one of the oldest Christmas carols, _Gaudete et exsultate (Rejoice and Be Glad)_,” Primiani says in a press release. “The piece weaves in all the familiar favorites. It was great fun for me to focus on something so joyful.” On December 7 at 7 p.m. ET, Primiani will participate in a [streamed conversation](link_26) with Music Director John Devlin. The “A Not-So-Silent Night with the WSO” program, performed at the Cathedral of St. Joseph in Wheeling, West Virginia, will include other holiday music in addition to the Primiani premiere.

## [Opinion: Our country needs a cabinet-level secretary of arts and culture](link_27)

Posted on December 7, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](link_1) - [News Briefs](link_9)

[](link_27)
“When a president calls a meeting of the Cabinet, most vital sectors of the economy—from soybean farmers to auto manufacturers—have an appointed government representative in the room, a secretary of agriculture or transportation, to speak for them,” writes Peter Marks in Wednesday’s (12/2) [_Washington Post_](link_28). “You know what doesn’t get a seat at the table, and never has? The arts. And in this crisis moment, when a pandemic threatens ruination for museums, theaters, concert halls, opera houses, dance studios, cineplexes and amusement parks—and the 5.1 million arts workers who staff them—the time has come to rectify this glaring oversight. Now, more than ever, we need a secretary of arts and culture…. The notion is gaining momentum among leaders and advocates of nonprofit groups and for-profit companies…. More than 50 nations designate an official in the top ranks of government whose portfolio includes nurturing artistic endeavors. In Germany, for instance, the minister of state for culture, Monika Grütters, has been an ardent proponent of aid to artists during the covid-19 crisis—a backing that helped secure a staggering $54 billion in aid for those in cultural, media and artistic pursuits.”

# General Information

403 N. Main Street | South Bend, Indiana 46601 | 574.234.1112 | www.sbct.org

**Box Office Hours**Monday-Friday: Noon – 6 PM, Saturday and Sunday: Closed  
On performance days, the Box Office will open 60 minutes prior to the start of the performance.

**Late Seating** Latecomers will be asked to wait for an appropriate time to enter the house and will be directed to seats at the discretion of the Guest Services Manager.

**Lost Tickets** If your tickets are lost or misplaced, the Box Office will gladly reissue them at no charge.

**Ticket Refunds** The CIVIC does not offer refunds to patrons but will be happy to move your ticket to another show.

**Parking** We offer free parking in the connected lot north of the building and around the circumference of the building.

**“Pay What You Can” Previews** The final dress rehearsal of most CIVIC productions is set aside for patrons who may not be able to afford a full-price ticket. Tickets are available 60 minutes before curtain on a first come, first served basis.

**Accessibility for Patrons with Special Needs**Please inform the CIVIC Box Office of any special needs while ordering tickets to ensure suitable accommodations can be arranged.

**Assisted Listening Devices** Listening devices are available free of charge. Please see the Guest Services Manager or Box Office staff prior to being seated. Devices are to be returned after the performance.

**Accessible Seating** If possible, please call the CIVIC Box Office 24 hours prior to arrival.

*   Accessible restroom is in the Main Level Lobby
*   Wheelchair accessible seating is available in Row E of the Wilson Auditorium, along with companion seat. Patrons will need to contact the Box Office in advance of the performance to ensure wheelchair seating availability.
*   Wider armless chairs are available for larger guests. Please contact the Box Office to reserve these seats in advance.

**Cancellation Policy**

The CIVIC reserves the right to cancel/postpone performances. The Executive Team will make this call at least four (4) hours before the performance time. In the event of cancellation, a message will be sent to the ticket purchaser’s email address. A cancellation notice will also be posted on the CIVIC’s Facebook page, and a website.  
If an event/performance is cancelled by the CIVIC:

*   Patrons should contact the Box Office to discuss ticketing options.
*   Production volunteers will coordinate with staff in an effort to reschedule cancelled  
performances as the schedule allows.

## [Oracle Gives $10 Million to Save Nashville Symphony’s 2026-27 Season](link_6)

Posted on October 5, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 2](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/schermerhorn.jpg)](https://symphony.org/oracle-gives-10-million-to-save-nashville-symphonys-2026-27-season/ [link_6])
In Sunday’s (10/4) [_Nashville Scene_](link_8), William Williams writes, “Just days after the financially strapped Nashville Symphony suspended its 2026-27 season and furloughed its musicians and staffers in an effort to erase a $10 million operating deficit, technology industry behemoth Oracle has stepped up to sustain the embattled nonprofit…. Oracle is investing $10 million in the organization in what is being called a ‘strategic partnership’ to help the Nashville Symphony establish firm fiscal footing and to keep the 2026-27 season intact. With the Oracle assistance, the nonprofit will be able to maintain its 27 full-time staff positions and all 77 orchestra members, thus avoiding a furlough that was announced on Sept. 29 and was to have begun on Oct. 18. ‘Oracle’s commitment is a lifeline for the Nashville Symphony and the community we serve,’ Mark Tillinger, Nashville Symphony’s newly named president and CEO, says … Tillenger was tapped to lead the nonprofit after Mark Cantrell stepped down as president and chief executive officer following a two-month tenure. Based in Austin, Oracle is currently constructing its future … global headquarters [in Nashville]…. Symphony officials said last week the organization’s cost structure and revenue base had become ‘increasingly misaligned’ as the institution had operated significantly on the generosity of [late donor Martha] Ingram.”

Tags:[Business and Finance](link_9), [Governance](link_10), [Grants and Funding](link_11)

## [Free League Webinar: “A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras”](link_12)

Posted on October 5, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 3](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/New_Board_Orientation_Webinar_Dec_2025_w_headshots.jpg)](https://symphony.org/free-league-webinar-a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2/ [link_12])
On Tuesday, October 6, the League of American Orchestras will present “[A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras,](link_13)”a free webinar designed specifically for new board members of orchestras. Simon Woods, President and CEO of the League of American Orchestras, and Doug Hagerman, the League’s immediate past board chair and former Chair of the Milwaukee Symphony, will provide an overview of the orchestra field, covering recent national trends, current opportunities, and challenges. They’ll also dive into aspects of governance unique to orchestras, among them managing complex leadership models and multiple stakeholder groups. They will also show how the League’s resources can support board members and connect them to a vibrant network of orchestras across the country. After the success of this new board member orientation in 2025, the League is making it an annual event and will continue to incorporate feedback from past sessions, shaping an event with useful and relevant insights.

“A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras” takes place on Tuesday, October 6, 3:00 p.m. Eastern / Noon Pacific Times. Questions? Contact League Member Services at[member@americanorchestras.org](mailto:member@americanorchestras.org).

Learn more and register for the free webinar at [https://americanorchestras.org/event/a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2026/](link_13).

Tags:[Business and Finance](link_9), [Digital and Streaming](link_14), [Governance](link_10), [Professional Development](link_15)

## [Milwaukee Symphony Returns to Rhinelander in Northern Wisconsin Tour](link_16)

Posted on October 5, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 4](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/milwaukee-sym-musicians.jpg)](https://symphony.org/milwaukee-symphony-returns-to-rhinelander-in-northern-wisconsin-tour/ [link_16])
In Wednesday’s (9/30) [WJFW](link_17) (Rhinelander, Wisconsin), Ethan Krinke reports, “The Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra used to come up to Rhinelander once per year, but eventually stopped due to logistical and scheduling challenges. Thanks to many organizations and private donors, the orchestra returned to Rhinelander this week to play for audiences of all ages in separate concerts…. The orchestra played for middle school students at Rhinelander High School on Wednesday morning. President of the orchestra, Mark Niehaus, knows that a performance like this could be the inspiration for young kids to become musicians. ‘For many of these kids, it’s going to be the first time they have heard a professional orchestra or even an orchestra period,’ Niehaus said…. For the middle school students, the orchestra gave them a taste of Beethoven, ‘William Tell’ Overture, music from ‘Harry Potter’ and ‘Wicked.’… Niehaus said, ‘Nowadays, so much music is electronic and premade and everything that happens on this stage with this orchestra happens in real time by real people with real instruments.’ The orchestra also played a full concert for the public on Tuesday and later played an intimate chamber concert at Nicolet College Wednesday. The orchestra plans to return to Rhinelander every year in the foreseeable future.”

[Video 1](link_18)

## [San Antonio Philharmonic Sues Former Music Director Jeffrey Kahane’s New Orchestra](link_22)

Posted on October 2, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 5](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/kahane-harmonium.jpg)](https://symphony.org/san-antonio-philharmonic-sues-former-music-director-jeffrey-kahanes-new-orchestra/ [link_22])
In Thursday’s (10/1) [_San Antonio Current_](link_23)(Texas), Sanford Nowlin writes, “Days before the public debut of the city’s newest orchestra, the Harmonium of Texas, the … San Antonio Philharmonic has sued the fledgling group in federal court, accusing its leader of fraud. Filed Tuesday, the lawsuit against the Harmonium of Texas and its founder, Jeffrey Kahane, accuses the conductor, pianist and educator of misleading the Philharmonic’s leadership when he resigned in February, midway through a three-year contract as musical director. The petition alleges Kahane stole ‘trade secrets’ during his time at the Phil … Neither Kahane nor the Harmonium of Texas, which will undertake its debut performance this Friday … were available for immediate comment. Kahane—who described himself in an earlier statement as a ‘significant donor’ to the Phil—parted ways after it was locked out of its primary performance venue … Tuesday’s suit accuses Kahane of fabricating a story that he was forced to resign from the Phil to return to full-time teaching at the University of Southern California … Harmonium’s concert this weekend, a performance of Carl Orff’s ‘Carmina Burana’ … is start of a season scheduled to include roughly 20 performances … The Philharmonic has yet to unveil a 2026-2027 concert season.”

Tags:[Business and Finance](link_9), [Conductors](link_24)

## [Atlanta Symphony Orchestra Music Director Nathalie Stutzmann on the Art of Making Art](link_25)

Posted on October 2, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 6](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/stutzmann-atlanta.jpg)](https://symphony.org/atlanta-symphony-orchestra-music-director-nathalie-stutzmann-on-the-art-of-making-art/ [link_25])
In Monday’s (9/28) [_Arts Atlanta_](link_26), James L. Paulk writes, “Nathalie Stutzmann, music director of the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra … discussed her vision for the ASO and her flourishing international career. ARTSATL: Let’s talk about the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra, where you’ve been music director for four years, and you recently renewed your contract for another three years…. You’ve just had a really successful season. What do you see as the biggest challenges going forward? STUTZMANN: I think it’s a permanent challenge—you should never think you arrived somewhere. Musicians are artisanal people. Every morning we have to try to do better…. My way is to every day restart, searching: What can we do better today?… Every day we wake up, we are different and the music has to be alive…. I am very lucky at this stage of my artistic life: I have the chance to conduct some of the best orchestras in the world…. But Atlanta is my main sport; it will stay my main sport…. I think it’s very obvious in our concerts: The joy of playing, the way the orchestra gives me so much energy and that goes to the audience—that touches our people.”

Tags:[Conductors](link_24), [Musicians](link_27)

## [Review: Los Angeles Chamber Orchestra Opens Season with Carlos Simon World Premiere, Kodaly, de Falla](link_28)

Posted on October 2, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 7](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/GinellLACOSimonHolidayConductor.jpg)](https://symphony.org/review-los-angeles-chamber-orchestra-opens-season-with-carlos-simon-world-premiere-kodaly-de-falla/ [link_28])
In Wednesday’s (9/30) [_Classical Voice North America_](link_29), Richard S. Ginell writes, “It didn’t take long to decode the meaning of ‘Movement(s),’ the umbrella title of the Los Angeles Chamber Orchestra’s first program of the 2026-27 season on Sept. 26. The ‘s’ in ‘Movement(s)’ revealed the motive behind both guest conductor Lina González-Granados’ and the marketing department’s strategy … ‘Movement’ can simply mean ‘dance’—and there was plenty of that to be heard in Kodaly’s _Dances of Galanta_ … and the Suite No. 1 from Falla’s ballet _El sombrero de tres picos_ … It also referred to the idea of a movement as a social force; hence, the world premiere of Carlos Simon’s _Afterparty_, a song cycle based on texts by poets aligned with the Harlem Renaissance…. _Afterparty_ is a gorgeous piece of music, full stop. Simon is not afraid to express himself in lush, songful terms with richly melodic lines for his singer, the astounding countertenor John Holiday, whose sweet, luscious timbre can easily be mistaken for that of a female soprano if your eyes are closed…. It’s hard to pinpoint a specific Simon sound, yet he does what he does with a sharp ear for color backed by plenty of craft…. [In _Afterparty_], it was enough on a sensual level but not on the totality of what this work could mean.”

Tags:[Composers](link_30), [Conductors](link_24), [Repertoire](link_31)

## [Minnesota Orchestra Opens Season with “Firebird” with Video Collage](link_32)

Posted on October 1, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 8](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/minneapolis-sondergard.jpg)](https://symphony.org/minnesota-orchestra-opens-season-with-firebird-with-video-collage/ [link_32])
In Saturday’s (9/26) [_Minnesota Star Tribune_](link_33), Rob Hubbard writes, “Minnesota Orchestra Music Director Thomas Søndergård seems to lean toward a ‘bigger the better’ approach in his programming … Could the occasional visitor or classical music newbie become a regular if it were a more stimulating visual experience? That seems to be the impetus behind the orchestra’s ‘Sound Unbound’ collaborations with video designers. For each, Orchestra Hall’s towering back wall of tumbling cubes can become a playground of the imagination … That’s what Søndergård and the orchestra offered Friday night to launch the orchestra’s 124th season … and it was an unqualified success. Igor Stravinsky’s complete, original 1910 music for the ballet, ‘The Firebird,’ was well played, full of finely sculpted ensemble work. And the video design of England’s Tal Rosner proved a fine complement to the music, subtly touching upon elements of the ballet … [In the finale], Søndergård and the orchestra produced a sound so exciting that it eclipsed whatever visuals had been created for the occasion.” Also on the program was Prokofiev’s Second Piano Concerto, “played with all the required virtuosity by Ukrainian pianist Vadym Kholodenko—and it proved a memorable opening night, full of big sounds and expansive emotions.”

Tags:[Artistic Planning](link_34), [Conductors](link_24), [Repertoire](link_31)

## [Fort Worth Symphony Premieres a New Arrangement of Brahms Concerto](link_35)

Posted on October 1, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](link_7) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 9](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/robert-spano-fort-worth.jpg)](https://symphony.org/fort-worth-symphony-premieres-a-new-arrangement-of-brahms-concerto/ [link_35])
In Saturday’s (9/26) [_Dallas Morning News_](link_36), Scott Cantrell writes, “Familiar composers Joseph Haydn and Johannes Brahms, born almost exactly a century apart, were paired in the Fort Worth Symphony Orchestra’s Friday night concert. But one of the pieces was presented in a world premiere arrangement…. The novelty, conducted by music director Robert Spano at Bass Performance Hall, was pianist Dejan Lazić’s piano-concerto arrangement of Brahms’ Double Concerto for violin and cello. A Croatian native trained in clarinet and composition as well as piano at the Salzburg Mozarteum, Lazić has composed original works as well as an earlier piano-concerto version of Brahms’ Violin Concerto. What’s billed as the Brahms/ Lazić Piano Concerto ‘No. 4’ leaves the orchestral score untouched but adapts the solo parts for more or less Brahmsian pianistic effects…. I rather enjoyed it. Lazić’s arrangement supplied pianistic sonorities that effectively filled in solo parts originally for just a violin and a cello. Whether unaccompanied or integrated within orchestral textures, the piano parts sounded plausibly Brahmsian to me…. Brahms was no stranger to rearrangements. He developed his Piano Concerto No. 1 from a two-piano sonata and an intermediate symphonic version. And he produced piano arrangements of all four of his symphonies…. Lazić played his Double Concerto arrangement with panache … The performance was personable and caringly formed, and violins produced a particularly lovely silvery sheen…. I rather like the current FWSO practice of introducing concerts with well-produced videos featuring members of the orchestra.”

Tags:[Composers](link_30), [Musicians](link_27), [Repertoire](link_31)

## [Ukrainian Freedom Orchestra performances in New York and Washington, D.C.](link_55)

Posted on August 8, 2022 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_55)
New York’s Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts will present two free concerts by the touring Ukrainian Freedom Orchestra on August 18 and 19 at Damrosch Park. The orchestra, organized by the Metropolitan Opera and Polish National Opera, is touring Europe and the U.S. this summer. Musicians in the orchestra include recent refugees of the war, members of orchestras in other parts of Europe, and musicians from ensembles in Kyiv, Lviv, Kharkiv, and Odesa. Canadian-Ukrainian conductor Keri-Lynn Wilson will lead the orchestra in Ukrainian composer Valentin Silvestrov’s Seventh Symphony and Chopin’s Piano Concerto No. 2, with Ukrainian pianist Anna Fedorova. Ukrainian soprano Liudmyla Monastyrska will perform “Abscheulicher!” from Beethoven’s _Fidelio_. An outdoor reception following the August 18 performance will offer an opportunity to connect with the Ukrainian artists. The concert is free, but donations are encouraged to organizations supporting the resettlement of Ukrainians. The Lincoln Center performance is a co-presentation of all eleven resident organizations; there will also be an August 20 performance at the Kennedy Center in Washington D.C. More information [here](link_56).

“Jen Luzzo has been hired by the Kennedy Center to oversee classical music public relations,” writes Nicholas Beard in Friday’s (8/5) [_Musical America_](link_58) (subscription required). “Previously in a related position with the New York Philharmonic, she arrived at the KenCen last week and has a portfolio that includes the Washington National Opera (WNO), the National Symphony Orchestra (NSO), the Fortas Chamber Music series, all music education activities—of which there are many—and initiatives that explore the intersection of music and wellness. Luzzo studied music and broadcast journalism at Syracuse University.”

# Author: Jennifer Melick

Jennifer Melick, _Symphony_ magazine’s former longtime managing editor, is a freelance journalist based in Detroit.

## [Cincinnati Symphony and Pops announce details of scaled-down in-person performances](link_6)

Posted on December 16, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_6)
“The Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra and Cincinnati Pops will soon be bringing back in-person performances for the first time since March,” writes Bill Cieslewicz in Tuesday’s (12/15) [_Cincinnati Business Courier_](link_7). “The CSO and Pops [plan] to replace all previously scheduled concerts at Music Hall from January through May 2021 with a new series of rescaled in-person concerts. In addition, the two groups will continue producing live stream programs to be premiered free and subsequently made available on-demand for subscribers and donors or on a pay-per-view basis for others. On Jan. 23, the orchestra will return to live performances for in-person audiences at Music Hall, though with a significantly reduced audience capacity under current [safety] protocols…. Music director Louis Langrée will conduct seven of the CSO’s 10 programs and Matthias Pintscher will officially begin his role as creative partner. Making their CSO subscription concert debuts are assistant conductor François López-Ferrer and guest conductor Ruth Reinhardt…. Pops conductor John Morris Russell will lead three Pops programs and the annual ‘Red White & Boom’ July 4th concert at Riverbend, while Pops principal guest conductor Damon Gupton will lead one program…. The Lollipops Family Concerts series will present one digital concert.”

## [Dayton Philharmonic, Opera, and Ballet revise 2020-21 programming, to launch Dec. 31 in person and virtually](link_8)

Posted on December 16, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_8)
“The Dayton Performing Arts Alliance announced all originally scheduled programming in its 2020-21 ‘Celebrate’ season will not go as planned,” writes Elizabeth Kyle in Sunday’s (12/12) [_Dayton Business Journal_](link_9) (OH). The organization, which includes the Dayton Philharmonic, Dayton Ballet, and Dayton Opera, “took a careful look about the types of programming that could be [safely] offered… ‘While we are cancelling many of our previously scheduled programs … we are thrilled to also be announcing our DPAA Reimagined Season 2020-21, with 11 new Dayton Ballet, Dayton Opera and Dayton Philharmonic programs,’ said President and CEO Pat McDonald. ‘Access to these performances can be purchased in three ways—via in-theatre tickets, live stream tickets, or a virtual streams membership.’ … Patrons can attend in-theatre performances with socially-distanced, sanitized seating at the Schuster Center and Victoria Theatre. Each performance will be between 50 and 90 minutes each with no intermission, and limited seating is available in each venue…. The season kicks off with its New Year’s Eve performance titled ‘A New Beginning,’ on Dec. 31 and continues into the summer.” In January, Music Director Neal Gittleman will lead the Dayton Philharmonic in Beethoven’s Symphony No. 8 and Florence Price’s Violin Concerto, with Concertmaster Jessica Hung as soloist.

## [Celebrating Beethoven in his 250th-birthday year—with virtual performances, books, and more](link_10)

Posted on December 16, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_10)

![Image 2](https://live-hub-american-orchestras.pantheonsite.io/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/800x400-Beethoven-statue-in-Bonn-Germany.png)
Ernst Julius Hähnel’s statue of Beethoven in the composer’s hometown of Bonn, Germany.

“On Wednesday, Ludwig van Beethoven’s birthday will be celebrated for the 250th time,” writes Mark Swed in Tuesday’s (12/15) [_Los Angeles Times_](link_11). “The COVID-19 pandemic may have forced the cancellation of thousands of Beethoven performances around the world, but they have been replaced by thousands of [virtual] performances…. A Philadelphia Orchestra stream this Beethoven birthday week will precede a Beethoven piano concerto with Missy Mazzoli’s terrific ‘Ecstatic Science.’ … Gustavo Dudamel ended the latest L.A. Phil Sound/Stage program by following the exuberant last movement of Beethoven’s Seventh Symphony with the exuberant ending of Gabriela Ortiz’s ‘Corporea.’ The shoe fit…. Violinist Gidon Kremer’s latest recording, ‘Searching for Beethoven,’ with cellist Mario Brunello and the Kremerata Baltica, begins with Brunello’s arrangement of ‘Muss es Sein? Es muss sein!,’ a 1970s song by anarchistic French chanteur Leo Ferre…. Thomas Ades … is recording a set of Beethoven symphonies interspersed with pieces by [Gerald] Barry…. Two books have come along this year that reveal the composer in an enlightening contemporary light,” _William Kinderman’s Beethoven: A Political Artist in Revolutionary Times_ and Paul Griffiths’ novel _Mr. Beethoven_. “Hardly a page goes by in either of these superbly written and complementary books without offering an unexpected reason to care about Beethoven.”

Read Ben Finane’s article evaluating the relevance of Beethoven today in [_Symphony_ magazine](link_12).

Now more than ever, there are many demands on your finances—and the League appreciates being among your philanthropic priorities.

## [Charleston Symphony’s healthcare and testing partnership with MUSC Health](link_17)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_17)
South Carolina’s Charleston Symphony Orchestra has launched a partnership with Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Health to provide COVID-19 testing and safety oversight for its 2020-21 season. In addition to providing guidance and safety protocols for rehearsals and performances, MUSC is organizing and administering SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic testing for more than 70 musicians and event staff before every CSO concert. As part of the new partnership, CSO ensembles performed on December 10 and 11 for MUSC Health staff and patients at various sites throughout the hospital campus, including the main university hospital lobby, Ashley River Tower Annex, and Shawn Jenkins Children’s Hospital cafeteria area. The Charleston Symphony has been performing concerts for reduced audiences at the Gaillard Center, with fewer than 360 patrons in the hall per concert; the orchestra’s concerts are also streamed.

## [Obituary: Arts and music philanthropist Peggy Starr, 100](link_18)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_18)
“Peggy (Giffen) Starr, a champion of the arts and culture, died Wednesday at age 100,” reads an unsigned obituary in Thursday’s (12/10) [_Republican_](link_19) (Springfield, MA). “She was born in New York City in 1920, the daughter of the late Anne and Lewis Giffen, who were active in cultural affairs. Her mother was secretary of the New York City Opera company. Peggy and her late husband, David Starr, were a team throughout their 76-year marriage…. They spent … their lives working to make Springfield a better community. Peggy was a tireless volunteer. She was active in a number of Springfield organizations, including the Springfield Symphony, WGBY, the region’s public television station, New England Public Radio, and the Springfield Museums Association…. From 1960 to 1977 Peggy was music editor at the _Long Island Press_, guiding critics who covered ballet, music, theater and movies. Even before they arrived in Massachusetts, Peggy joined the Springfield Symphony. In 2007 … Peggy was honored with the Springfield Symphony Orchestra’s Janee Armstrong Friedmann Award [for her fundraising efforts]. Peggy is survived by their two children, Pamela Starr Bromberg … and her son Peter … and two grandchildren.”

## [Study in Barcelona conducts rapid antigen tests for volunteer audience](link_20)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_20)
“Eager for a live music show after months of social distancing, more than 1,000 Barcelona residents gathered Saturday to participate in a medical study to evaluate the effectiveness of same-day coronavirus screening to safely hold cultural events,” write Joseph Wilson and Emilio Morenatti in Saturday’s (12/12) [Associated Press](link_21). “After passing an antigen screening, 500 of the volunteers were randomly selected to enjoy a free concert inside Barcelona’s Apolo Theater. The other 500 who didn’t get selected were sent home. They will form a control group…. Antigen tests … produce results in 15 minutes.… The study is organized by Barcelona’s Fight AIDS and Infectious Diseases Foundation along with the Primavera Sound music festival…. Dr. Boris Revollo, the virologist who designed the study’s protocols, … insisted that the use of same-day antigen screening for large events wasn’t a substitute for face masks and other sanitation rules, but he believed it could be a powerful tool to help make large events safe enough until vaccines are widespread enough to beat back COVID-19.… The 500 allowed into the five-hour music festival … had to wear FFP2 face masks and use hand disinfectant…. All 1,000 of the volunteers will also undergo two PCR tests.”

## [Opinion: Boston Symphony’s BSO NOW concerts offer vision for post-pandemic future](link_22)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_22)
“The Boston Symphony Orchestra has rolled out a season of video offerings for a virtual audience, which it has dubbed ‘BSO NOW,’ ” writes Zoë Madonna in Friday’s (12/11) [_Boston Globe_](link_23). “BSO NOW programs are concerts for the time of coronavirus and all that entails…. The repertoire is for small ensembles … and each concert includes a chamber piece sans conductor and a short video feature…. BSO NOW is the BSO for ‘now’ in another sense of the word…. One of three BSO NOW concerts also puts Black Americans and their music front and center. This program is conducted and warmly annotated by BSO youth and family concerts conductor Thomas Wilkins, who has taken a much more visible role in the organization this year…. It’ll be a happy day when this isolated phase of the ‘now’ belongs firmly to the past, but some elements of BSO NOW should not be left behind…. That includes the focus on music by living composers as well as composers who have been passed over in the mainstream orchestral repertoire; the greater context given to the pieces; the welcoming, unpresumptuous atmosphere—all of these are essential not just for this now, but for when the future becomes now.”

## [R. Douglas Sheldon, formerly of Columbia Artists, starts artist management agency](link_24)

Posted on December 14, 2020 by [Jennifer Melick](https://symphony.org/author/jennifermelick/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[](link_24)
“It’s been just over 18 months since R. Douglas Sheldon … left Columbia Artists as its chairman and just over three months since that onetime behemoth of a classical music agency subsequently went belly up,” writes Susan Elliott in Thursday’s (12/11) [_Musical America_](link_25). “Now Sheldon is back, as the managing partner of Sheldon Artists, LLC, and managing many of the artists he worked with during his five decades at CAMI. Leading the conductor roster is Valery Gergiev, along with the Mariinsky Theater, of which Gergiev is artistic and general director. At the top of the violinists list is the previously announced Anne-Sophie Mutter, as well as rising young Dutch violinist Simone Lamsma…. Sheldon has signed Lera Auerbach as a conductor and composer as well as pianist.” Others signed by the agency include “Finnish conductor Eva Ollikainen, music and artistic director of the Iceland Symphony…. French conductor … Laurence Equilbey… American conductor Robert Trevino, music director of the Basque National Orchestra and chief conductor of the Malmö Symphony Orchestra … and the Royal Philharmonic under Vasily Petrenko … Sheldon, who has been instrumental in nurturing the careers of hundreds of major artists, identifies himself simply as founder and managing partner.”

## [Memphis Symphony: fresh spins on holiday traditions, including filmed “Nutcracker” with Ballet Memphis](link_26)

On Friday, “Their film _Nutcracker: A Gift from Ballet Memphis_ hits screens all over the country…. ‘It was a challenge,’ Gretchen Wollert McLennon, President and CEO of Ballet Memphis, said…. The orchestra is even continuing one of [its] holiday traditions. ‘_Magic of Memphis_ is a beloved tradition…. It’s a smaller production than we’ve done in past years. In some ways, it’s even more special … to people who are able to make it to the concert.’ _Magic of Memphis_ will be limited to only 15 percent capacity. ###### News Brief

##### December 16, 2020

# Dayton Philharmonic, Opera, and Ballet revise 2020-21 programming, to launch Dec. 31 in person and virtually

Share

[Facebook](https://symphony.org/#facebook "Facebook")[Twitter](https://symphony.org/#twitter "Twitter")

Change font size

[A Decrease font size.](https://symphony.org/dayton-philharmonic-opera-and-ballet-revise-2020-21-programming-to-launch-dec-31-in-person-and-virtually/# "Decrease font size")[A Reset font size.](https://symphony.org/dayton-philharmonic-opera-and-ballet-revise-2020-21-programming-to-launch-dec-31-in-person-and-virtually/# "Reset font size")[A Increase font size.](https://symphony.org/dayton-philharmonic-opera-and-ballet-revise-2020-21-programming-to-launch-dec-31-in-person-and-virtually/# "Increase font size")

“The Dayton Performing Arts Alliance announced all originally scheduled programming in its 2020-21 ‘Celebrate’ season will not go as planned,” writes Elizabeth Kyle in Sunday’s (12/12) [_Dayton Business Journal_](https://www.bizjournals.com/dayton/news/2020/12/12/dayton-performing-arts-alliance-cancels-shows.html) (OH). The organization, which includes the Dayton Philharmonic, Dayton Ballet, and Dayton Opera, “took a careful look about the types of programming that could be [safely] offered… ‘While we are cancelling many of our previously scheduled programs … we are thrilled to also be announcing our DPAA Reimagined Season 2020-21, with 11 new Dayton Ballet, Dayton Opera and Dayton Philharmonic programs,’ said President and CEO Pat McDonald. ‘Access to these performances can be purchased in three ways—via in-theatre tickets, live stream tickets, or a virtual streams membership.’ … Patrons can attend in-theatre performances with socially-distanced, sanitized seating at the Schuster Center and Victoria Theatre. Each performance will be between 50 and 90 minutes each with no intermission, and limited seating is available in each venue…. The season kicks off with its New Year’s Eve performance titled ‘A New Beginning,’ on Dec. 31 and continues into the summer.” In January, Music Director Neal Gittleman will lead the Dayton Philharmonic in Beethoven’s Symphony No. 8 and Florence Price’s Violin Concerto, with Concertmaster Jessica Hung as soloist.

# About Us

### The South Bend Civic Theatre Aims to enrich and create community through live theatre.

## Our STORY

South Bend Civic Theatre (SBCT) was founded in 1957 by two University of Notre Dame graduates who believed community theatre should be an important part of this area’s culture, and who also believed that living in our community were aspiring actors and actresses who needed to show and form their talents.

While early performances were held in homes, hotels, and various locations at Notre Dame, SBCT staged most of its productions after 1968 at the Firehouse, a local historic landmark located on Portage Ave, in South Bend’s historic Near Northwest neighborhood.

Beginning in 2000, SBCT began staging larger productions outside the Firehouse, and exploring options for a new permanent venue. In January 2007, the beginning of the Civic’s 50th Anniversary year, SBCT celebrated the opening of its new home in the heart of downtown South Bend, in what had formerly been a First Church of Christ Scientist. The historic domed structure is an architectural wonder and sealed SBCT’s position as a pillar of the region’s art community.

WE PLEDGE TO BE

![Image 3](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/spotlight-150x150.png)

A light to illuminate the darkness

![Image 4](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/fire-150x150.png)

A flame to ignite curiosity and imagination

![Image 5](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/lighthouse-150x150.png)

A beacon to guide all toward hope, unity, and understanding

### “Theatre is about finding yourself, whether you’re in the audience or on the stage. Theatre allows you a blank space to discover who you really are and, hopefully, become the best version of who you are. It’s a rare and beautiful thing.”

_Aaron Nichols, Executive Director_

The CIVIC enriches and creates community through three pillars:

### EXCELLENCE  
 EDUCATION  
 EQUITY

Wednesday, November 18 | 6:00pm  
Civic Main Lobby

A warm Southern comedy about friendship, second chances, and starting over.

A group of longtime friends who gather at Spa-Dee-Dah, an abandoned church-turned-day spa in the small Southern town of Eden Falls. When Sugar Lee decides to renovate the place and turn it into a retreat, the women find themselves dealing with a series of personal and romantic complications.

As old relationships, new romances, family issues, and long-held secrets surface, the women lean on one another—and prove that friendship can get you through just about anything. Along the way, there are plenty of laughs, colorful characters, and a little bit of Southern sass.

### CULTIVATING THE WHOLE ARTIST: MIND, BODY, AND SOUL.

## MORE THAN A STAGE

South Bend Civic Theatre is more than a building where productions are staged. It is a community space where dialogue is fostered. Our educational programs introduce people of all ages to theatre. We work with elementary students taking an acting class for the first time and senior citizens who want to try something new.

Our educational programs allow more of our community to experience the power of theatre. We offer outstanding theatre training and experiences by a team of professional, seasoned instructors who cultivate an environment of trust, collaboration, and mutual respect.

[Video 1](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/sbct_gala-2026-1080p.mp4)

[](https://sbct.org/education/#)

## FIELD TRIP OPPORTUNITIES

**Generously supported by Shein Trust**

South Bend Civic Theatre is proud to present productions that will encourage curiosity in every member of our community. Our Theatre for Young Audience (TYA) productions allow us to produce DYNAMIC theatre at a fraction of the cost for our area schools. Jump in, see what all the excitement is about, and allow your students to absorb the powerful messages that each of these productions convey.

[Field Trips](https://sbct.org/field-trip/)

## UPCOMING CLASSES

SESSIONS RUN September - May
## NOW ENROLLING: CIVIC Classes

For GRADES K- ADULT

[Youth Classes](https://sbct.org/youth-classes/)

[Adult Classes](https://sbct.org/adult-18-classes-2/)

### “We’ve really started focusing on building compassion and empathy within the kids. Not just from the standpoint that they can use it for their acting, but it also teaches them how to be connected citizens. And isn’t that kind of the purpose of theatre?”

#### -Joshua Napierkowski

![Image 3: Lion King, Jr.](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/SBCT-field-trip-5-scaled.jpg)

![Image 4: Beauty and the Beast](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/071826_BeautyandtheBeast_Civic_0385-scaled.jpg)

![Image 5: Beauty and the Beast](https://sbct.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/071826_BeautyandtheBeast_Civic_0481-scaled.jpg)

[EDUCATION PROGRAMS](https://sbct.org/education/)

## **A FLAME TO IGNITE CURIOUSITY  
THEATRE FOR YOUNG AUDIENCES**

## Theatre for Young Audiences was launched in 2009 as a series of developmentally appropriate shows each season. These productions are dedicated to cultivating curiosity and exposure to the arts. The focus of TYA is to offer a theatre experience to everyone, no matter their background. Each year, students from across the South Bend area and larger region enjoy TYA performances for a reduced cost of $10 per student, or half of that for Title 1 schools. In 2019, more than 9,000 elementary and middle school students enjoyed TYA productions.

## **A BEACON TO GUIDE ALL TOWARDS HOPE  
CLASSES & THE COMPANY**

## SBCT’s Classes provides a year-round curriculum for students in grades K-12 who have an interest in theatre. Members attend workshops in acting, improvisation, movement, and voice. They also experience the business of acting, including auditioning, scene study, dance, and singing. Research into SAT scores shows that students involved in drama performance perform better on the exam. Involvement in the arts has also been shown to increase student engagement, particularly for students considered to be at high risk for dropping out of high school. Students who participate in the arts are also three more times more likely to win an award for school attendance than those who do not.

**LEARN MORE:**

[Educational Resources](https://sbct.org/resource-materials/)

## **A LIGHT TO ILLUMINATE THE DARKNESS  
STUDENT OUTREACH**The South Bend Civic Theatre aims to show young students how theatre and other performing arts play an important role in sparking conversation around social issues. Most recently, the CIVIC’s student outreach team has developed an in-depth curriculum for high schools to introduce students to August Wilson. The CIVIC is poised to become one of the few theatres in the country to produce Wilson’s full American Century Cycle, and CIVIC staff created an 82-page curriculum to be used by high school instructors as they introduced their students to the first play in the series, “Gem of the Ocean.”

# [The Future of the Art Form](https://symphony.org/features/the-future-of-the-art-form/)

What’s in store for orchestras, musicians, composers, audiences? Howard Herring, who recently completed 25 years as president and CEO of New World Symphony, looks ahead.

![Image 8: Thomas Wilkins leads a BSO NOW program with Duke Ellington, William Grant Still, and much more.](https://bostonglobe-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/resizer/v2/ADLCUJ6D45A65JMRKVY5RAPCNQ.jpg?auth=ad88de8c7addc046c60f3914456cc98843094abc9f604348683c89d5ddfc8501&width=1440)

Thomas Wilkins leads a BSO NOW program with Duke Ellington, William Grant Still, and much more.Aram Boghosian/Courtesy Boston Symphony Orchestra

“Now” is a slippery word. The instant I finish typing it, the “now” in which my fingers pressed the keys has zipped into the past never to return, with a new “now” arisen to take its place. “Now” moves quickly — or so it would be nice to believe in our collective and claustrophobic “now,” a “now” that seems to drag longer every time we look up. And so the Boston Symphony Orchestra has rolled out a season of video offerings for a virtual audience, which it has dubbed “BSO NOW.” This is the BSO for now; the BSO, for now.

Practically speaking, BSO NOW programs are concerts for the time of coronavirus and all that entails. The stage of Symphony Hall once again welcomes BSO musicians, but the repertoire is for small ensembles or individual sections, and each concert includes a chamber piece sans conductor and a short video feature; rehearsals need not be as long or crowded. Watching the players, they perform as if every piece may be their last till who knows when — because every piece may be. For the moment, indoor gatherings up to a certain size are allowed. But as the number of new COVID cases and the percentage of positive tests ticks ominously upward, and with Governor Baker rolling back the state’s reopening this week, one can’t help but wonder: : Could this be the only BSO we’ll see for now, before Symphony Hall goes silent again? Are we seeing a light at the end of the tunnel, or are we facing down an oncoming train?

## [Free League Webinar: “A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras”](https://symphony.org/free-league-webinar-a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2/ "Free League Webinar: “A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras”")

Posted on October 5, 2026 by [Talia Shulze](https://symphony.org/author/taliashulze/) - [News Briefs](https://symphony.org/category/news-briefs/)

[![Image 2](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/New_Board_Orientation_Webinar_Dec_2025_w_headshots.jpg)](https://symphony.org/free-league-webinar-a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2/)
On Tuesday, October 6, the League of American Orchestras will present “[A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras,](https://americanorchestras.org/event/a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2026/)”a free webinar designed specifically for new board members of orchestras. Simon Woods, President and CEO of the League of American Orchestras, and Doug Hagerman, the League’s immediate past board chair and former Chair of the Milwaukee Symphony, will provide an overview of the orchestra field, covering recent national trends, current opportunities, and challenges. They’ll also dive into aspects of governance unique to orchestras, among them managing complex leadership models and multiple stakeholder groups. They will also show how the League’s resources can support board members and connect them to a vibrant network of orchestras across the country. After the success of this new board member orientation in 2025, the League is making it an annual event and will continue to incorporate feedback from past sessions, shaping an event with useful and relevant insights.

“A New Board Member’s Guide to the Landscape of American Orchestras” takes place on Tuesday, October 6, 3:00 p.m. Eastern / Noon Pacific Times. Questions? Contact League Member Services at[member@americanorchestras.org](mailto:member@americanorchestras.org).

Learn more and register for the free webinar at [https://americanorchestras.org/event/a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2026/](https://americanorchestras.org/event/a-new-board-members-guide-to-the-landscape-of-american-orchestras-2026/).

Around 300,000 tickets were sold for Proms performances at the Royal Albert Hall and venues across the UK, including over 72,000 £8 Promming tickets…. Sam Jackson, Controller, BBC Radio 3 and BBC Proms, says: ‘The BBC Proms exists to bring the joy of live music to as many people as possible, and it’s hugely encouraging to see audiences continuing to grow.’ ”

[![Image 5](https://symphony.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/plano-recording.jpg)](https://symphony.org/local-composers-and-focus-for-plano-symphonys-first-recording/)
In Monday’s (8/17) [_Local Profile_](https://www.localprofile.com/arts-culture/plano-symphony-orchestra-signs-first-recording-deal-with-grammy-winning-label-12673328)(Plano, TX), Ruth Alcivar writes, “For more than four decades, the Plano Symphony Orchestra has brought music to audiences across North Texas. Now, for the first time, some of the music created through and connected to the orchestra is preparing to reach listeners around the world. The Plano Symphony Orchestra has signed its first recording deal with Grammy Award-winning label Reference Recordings. The album will be recorded Aug. 17–20 at the Meyerson Symphony Center under Maestro Héctor Guzmán, with international distribution planned in more than 25 countries. But rather than using its recording debut to revisit familiar classical standards, PSO is building the album around commissioned works and composers with ties to the orchestra and North Texas, essentially preserving a piece of its own musical legacy while introducing it to a much larger audience. That connection is apparent from the album’s opening track: Plano Overture. The piece was written by Marcos Lifshitz, who became PSO’s inaugural composer-in-residence for the 2025–26 season. Plano Overture premiered with the orchestra on Oct. 18, 2025, and will now become part of its first commercial recording. The album also includes works by Robert Xavier Rodriguez, Xi Wang, Quinn Mason and David Guion, along with ‘Ciana’ by three-time Grammy winner Branford Marsalis…. PSO President and CEO Gregory Patterson said … ‘This recording project is the next step in expanding our footprint beyond North Texas and is a milestone for this orchestra and the city of Plano.’ ”

Abbott, the medical technology giant outside Chicago, and Blood Centers of America have devised a workaround for people like me—prime donation candidates, but fearful … In 32 countries and at 75 sites in the United States, blood donors can put on a Samsung Galaxy XR headset and choose between two interactive, mixed-reality games … Developed by the San Francisco-based Rock Paper Reality, both games are the brainchild of Miguel Carrazza Morales, a product manager at Abbott … Carrazza’s goal is to create ‘an experience for everyone’ to bring in as many donors as possible … That experience extends to the games’ soundtracks [by Joe Clark]. Abbott commissioned the Chicago Symphony Orchestra … to record them. It was the first time this august ensemble has ventured into music for video games or interactive media…. Abbott commissioned the Chicago Symphony Orchestra … to record them. It was the first time this august ensemble has ventured into music for video games or interactive media…. [Video 1](https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/entertainment/music/2020/12/07/south-bend-symphony-local-arts-groups-to-collaborate-for-online-conce/116062114/)

SOUTH BEND — The South Bend Symphony Orchestra, South Bend Civic Theatre and other local performing arts groups are collaborating on an online holiday concert to premiere at 7 p.m. Dec. 19, at southbendsymphony.org/LOC and sbct.org/LOC.

Titled “Light One Candle: A South Bend Community Celebration,” it explores the traditions of five cultural groups — Jewish, African American, Pokagon Band of Potawatomi, Latinx and Eastern Orthodox — through dance, storytelling and symphonic music.

As part of the video presentation, the public is invited to submit videos of themselves and loved ones holding a single candle. Video submissions should be 5-7 seconds in length, with no audio, and are due by Saturday at sbct.org/candlevideo.

After the video premieres, it will be available to the public until Jan. 6.
